paras.en: “We’re talking about a vaccine that has protected generations of children from a potentially devastating infection,” said study co-author Demetre Daskalakis, chief medical officer at Callen-Lorde and former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Illness, in the same statement. “And now we’re seeing fewer newborns receive it—even those we know are at greatest risk. These numbers aren’t just a trend line. Each data point represents a real child who may be left vulnerable to a preventable disease. At a time when vaccine policy is changing, we need more evidence guiding our decisions, not less.”
paras.zh: 研究报告合著者、卡伦洛德医院首席医疗官、美国疾病控制与预防中心国家免疫和呼吸系统疾病中心前主任德米特·达斯卡拉基斯 (Demetre Daskalakis) 在同一份声明中表示：“我们正在谈论一种可以保护几代儿童免受潜在毁灭性感染的疫苗。” “现在我们看到越来越少的新生儿接受疫苗接种，即使是那些我们知道面临最大风险的新生儿也是如此。这些数字不仅仅是一条趋势线。每个数据点都代表了一个可能容易感染可预防疾病的真实儿童。在疫苗政策发生变化的时候，我们需要更多而不是更少的证据来指导我们的决策。”

articles.title: Lightning strikes could more than double by 2100 thanks to climate change

paras.en: Lightning strikes could soon become so commonplace that we’ll need a new metaphor for rarity. In a new study published in Earth’s Future on Tuesday, researchers find “cloud-to-ground” lightning strikes—bolts that hit Earth’s surface—could more than double by 2100 compared with historical levels. And the reason is our warming world.
paras.zh: 闪电袭击可能很快就会变得如此普遍，以至于我们需要一个新的比喻来形容稀有性。在周二《地球未来》杂志上发表的一项新研究中，研究人员发现，到 2100 年，“云对地”雷击（击中地球表面的闪电）可能比历史水平增加一倍以上。原因是我们的世界正在变暖。

paras.en: Lightning is already becoming more common: between 1995 and 2014, the researchers found, lightning across the world increased by 11 percent compared with the early 20th century. In the coming years, it could jump by between 76 percent and 140 percent over the 1995–2014 period, much more than previous estimates suggest.
paras.zh: 闪电已经变得越来越普遍：研究人员发现，从 1995 年到 2014 年，全世界的闪电比 20 世纪初增加了 11%。未来几年，1995 年至 2014 年期间这一数字可能会跃升 76% 至 140%，远高于之前的估计。

paras.en: “I was quite surprised that the projections were so high,” said the study’s lead author Andreas Krause, who studies Earth sciences modeling at the Technical University of Munich, in a statement. “I expected smaller changes.”
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、慕尼黑工业大学研究地球科学模型的安德烈亚斯·克劳斯（Andreas Krause）在一份声明中表示：“我对预测如此之高感到非常惊讶。” “我预计会有较小的变化。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The reason has to do with how lightning forms: as thunderstorm clouds develop, positively charged particles collect near the top of the cloud while negatively charged particles amass near the bottom. According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, most lightning occurs inside these clouds. But sometimes negatively charged particles in the cloud can connect with positively charged particles on the ground, generating a thunderbolt—or “cloud-to-ground” lightning.
paras.zh: 原因与闪电的形成方式有关：随着雷暴云的形成，带正电的粒子聚集在云的顶部附近，而带负电的粒子则聚集在云的底部附近。根据国家海洋和大气管理局的说法，大多数闪电发生在这些云层内。但有时云中的带负电的粒子可以与地面上的带正电的粒子连接，产生雷电或“云对地”闪电。

paras.en: How dangerous lightning is depends somewhat on where you live. In the U.S. lightning strikes kill an average of 21 people per year and cause an estimated 24,600 fires per year. Countries such as India see a disproportionately high number of lightning strikes each year.
paras.zh: 闪电的危险程度在一定程度上取决于您居住的地方。在美国，雷击每年平均造成 21 人死亡，估计每年会引发 24,600 起火灾。印度等国家每年遭受雷击的次数异常多。

paras.en: As the climate warms, the study authors found, heat rising from Earth’s surface is more prone to shake up the atmosphere, creating more potential for electric fields—and cloud-to-ground lightning—to form.
paras.zh: 研究作者发现，随着气候变暖，从地球表面升起的热量更容易震动大气，从而为形成电场和云对地闪电创造更多可能性。

paras.en: Places with cooler climates, such as Alaska, stand to see the greatest rate of increase in lightning from previous levels. Other research suggests that lightning in the Arctic has tripled in recent years.
paras.zh: 气候较凉爽的地方，例如阿拉斯加，闪电的增幅将比之前的水平最高。其他研究表明，近年来北极的闪电数量增加了两倍。

articles.title: How do tumors talk to nerves? This scientist is finding out
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Sebnem Ece Eksi did a double take. Proteins typically studied in the brain were turning up in prostate cancer cells from high-risk patients. These proteins, called neuronal adhesion molecules, play a key role in the circuitry associated with memory.
paras.zh: Sebnem Ece Eksi 愣了一下。通常在大脑中研究的蛋白质出现在高危患者的前列腺癌细胞中。这些蛋白质被称为神经元粘附分子，在与记忆相关的电路中发挥着关键作用。

paras.en: The finding, made during her Ph.D. days at the University of Illinois Chicago, raised so many questions to which Eksi is still seeking answers. Now at the Oregon Health & Science University in Portland, Eksi has made it her lab’s goal to find out how nervous systems communicate with cancer. What were once two separate fields might be connected more closely than previously thought.
paras.zh: 这一发现是她在攻读博士学位期间做出的。在伊利诺伊大学芝加哥分校的几天里，提出了很多问题，而 Eksi 仍在寻找答案。现在，在波特兰的俄勒冈健康与科学大学，埃克西的实验室目标是找出神经系统如何与癌症沟通。曾经两个独立的领域之间的联系可能比之前想象的更加紧密。

paras.en: “What we’re learning is that tumors are actively communicating with the nervous system,” Eksi says. “In a way, it makes sense to me that a growing tumor in our bodies, in an organ, would be immediately sensed and detected by the nervous system.”
paras.zh: “我们了解到，肿瘤正在与神经系统积极沟通，”埃克西说。 “在某种程度上，对我来说，神经系统会立即感知和检测到我们体内某个器官中不断生长的肿瘤，这是有道理的。”

paras.en: Eksi now plans to test an AI image-based recognition algorithm to identify nerve fibers in human patients. This is exciting, she says, because these nerves aren’t normally visible in patient tumors. But through biopsies, she hopes to map out and observe how the nervous system — which impacts sleep, cognition and pain — changes as cancer progresses. The implications are significant, she says. Could experts use the nervous system to detect cancer early? Can they improve patients’ quality of life?
paras.zh: Eksi 现在计划测试一种基于人工智能图像的识别算法，以识别人类患者的神经纤维。她说，这很令人兴奋，因为这些神经在患者肿瘤中通常不可见。但通过活检，她希望了解并观察影响睡眠、认知和疼痛的神经系统如何随着癌症的进展而变化。她说，其影响是重大的。专家能否利用神经系统早期发现癌症？它们能改善患者的生活质量吗？

paras.en: “This field of cancer neuroscience can change all different stages of cancer diagnosis and treatments,” Eksi says. “It’s growing so quickly, the field itself.”
paras.zh: “癌症神经科学这一领域可以改变癌症诊断和治疗的所有不同阶段，”埃克西说。 “这个领域本身发展得非常快。”

articles.title: Motion under the ocean explains the depth of the world’s deepest spot
articles.author: Carolyn Gramling

paras.en: Challenger Deep is the deepest valley in the deepest trench in the ocean, plunging to roughly 11,000 meters below sea level.
paras.zh: 挑战者深渊 (Challenger Deep) 是海洋最深海沟中最深的山谷，深度约低于海平面 11,000 米。

paras.en: Now, scientists have a new clue about how it got to be so … well, deep.
paras.zh: 现在，科学家们找到了关于它如何变得如此……嗯，深的新线索。

paras.en: Challenger Deep is found within the Mariana Trench, a crescent-shaped gouge in the seafloor east of the Philippines in the Pacific Ocean. The trench is the scene of a slo-mo tectonic collision called a subduction zone: The Pacific plate is diving beneath the Mariana plate, bending downward as it sinks into the mantle, forming a steep trench on the ocean floor.
paras.zh: 挑战者深渊位于马里亚纳海沟内，马里亚纳海沟是菲律宾东部太平洋海底的一个新月形凿痕。海沟是慢速构造碰撞的场景，称为俯冲带：太平洋板块潜入马里亚纳板块下方，在沉入地幔时向下弯曲，在海底形成陡峭的海沟。

paras.en: All subduction zones are deep, but “it’s interesting why this is the deepest spot in the Earth’s ocean,” says geoscientist Robert Stern, an emeritus professor at the University of Texas at Dallas and a visiting researcher at the University of California, Los Angeles.
paras.zh: 所有俯冲带都很深，但“有趣的是，为什么这里是地球海洋最深的地方”，德克萨斯大学达拉斯分校名誉教授、加州大学洛杉矶分校客座研究员地球科学家罗伯特·斯特恩说。

paras.en: He and colleagues employed a remotely operated robot called ROV Jason/Medea to descend to more than 6,000 meters and explore the Mariana Trench seafloor around the edges of Challenger Deep. The rocks turned out to contain pyroclastic deposits, evidence of an erstwhile explosive volcanic eruption. Those deposits included platelike blocks that could indicate eruption pulses, and lobe-shaped rocks where the volcanic flows ended and quickly cooled.
paras.zh: 他和同事使用名为 ROV Jason/Medea 的远程操作机器人下降到 6,000 多米深处，探索挑战者深渊边缘的马里亚纳海沟海底。事实证明，这些岩石中含有火山碎屑沉积物，这是昔日火山喷发的证据。这些沉积物包括可以指示喷发脉冲的板状块体，以及火山流结束并迅速冷却的叶状岩石。

paras.en: These are the deepest pyroclastic deposits found on Earth, the scientists report November 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science.
paras.zh: 科学家们于 11 月 23 日在《地球科学前沿》上报告称，这些是地球上发现的最深的火山碎屑沉积物。

paras.en: How explosive an eruption is at Earth’s surface depends on the chemical makeup of the magma. When the molten rock contains a high proportion of volatile gases, including water vapor, those gases suddenly expand when the magma reaches the surface, producing a violent explosion.
paras.zh: 地球表面喷发的爆炸性取决于岩浆的化学成分。当熔岩含有高比例的挥发性气体（包括水蒸气）时，当岩浆到达地表时，这些气体会突然膨胀，产生剧烈的爆炸。

paras.en: Such explosive volcanism shouldn’t be possible in the deep sea; the pressure is too high for any escaping gases to expand, Stern says. Along with that mystery, the volcanic deposits were found unusually close to the trench, compared with what would be expected for a subduction zone.
paras.zh: 这种爆发性的火山活动在深海中是不可能发生的；斯特恩说，压力太高，任何逸出的气体都无法膨胀。除了这个谜团之外，与预期的俯冲带相比，火山沉积物的发现异常靠近海沟。

paras.en: Stern and his colleagues developed a hypothesis that incorporates these disparate pieces of evidence: The extreme depth of Challenger Deep, they say, may be at least partially due to an especially sharp bend in the Pacific Plate as it sinks into the mantle.
paras.zh: 斯特恩和他的同事提出了一个包含这些不同证据的假设：他们说，挑战者深渊的极端深度可能至少部分归因于太平洋板块在沉入地幔时发生的特别急剧的弯曲。

paras.en: That tighter bend would explain why volcanism is happening closer to the subduction zone than usual. The classic subduction zone scenario is that the sinking plate heats up and melts partially as it descends; the magma rises through the overhanging plate and erupts, forming volcanic island arcs several hundred kilometers from the collision zone. Here, the volcanic deposits were just a hundred kilometers or so from the trench — which makes sense if the plate is dipping more steeply.
paras.zh: 这种更紧的弯曲可以解释为什么火山活动发生在比平常更靠近俯冲带的地方。典型的俯冲带情景是下沉板块在下降时升温并部分熔化；岩浆穿过悬垂的板块上升并喷发，形成距碰撞区数百公里的火山岛弧。这里的火山沉积物距离海沟仅一百公里左右——如果板块倾斜得更陡的话，这是有道理的。

paras.en: As for the pyroclastics, “we can’t answer if the eruptions were really explosive,” Stern says. But at those pressures, any gases such as water vapor contained in the magma wouldn’t be able to explosively expand as they would at the surface.
paras.zh: 至于火山碎屑，“我们无法回答火山喷发是否真的具有爆炸性，”斯特恩说。但在这些压力下，岩浆中含有的任何气体（例如水蒸气）都无法像在地表那样爆炸性膨胀。

paras.en: Instead, the pyroclastic rocks might have formed through a new version of deep-sea eruption, one in which water emerging from the magma is initially in a supercritical fluid state. That would minimize any explosive expansion during the eruption and could also produce fragmented, dense deposits like those seen by Jason/Medea.
paras.zh: 相反，火山碎屑岩可能是通过一种新的深海喷发形成的，其中从岩浆中喷出的水最初处于超临界流体状态。这将最大限度地减少火山喷发期间的爆炸性扩张，并且还可能产生像杰森/美狄亚所看到的那样碎片化、致密的沉积物。

paras.en: The discovery of deep-sea pyroclastics is “surprising and unprecedented,” says William Chadwick, a geologist at Oregon State University in Newport. Challenger Deep may be the only place on Earth “with the ingredients to produce explosive volcanism in the super-deep ocean,” he says. “Imagining this happening is … pretty mind-boggling.”
paras.zh: 俄勒冈州立大学纽波特分校的地质学家威廉·查德威克表示，深海火山碎屑岩的发现“令人惊讶且前所未有”。他说，挑战者深渊可能是地球上唯一一个“拥有在超深海中产生爆炸性火山活动的成分”的地方。 “想象这种情况发生……真是令人难以置信。”

paras.en: A lot more work remains to be done to evaluate all of these new ideas, Stern says. “But a lot of things are now coming together.”
paras.zh: 斯特恩说，评估所有这些新想法还有很多工作要做。 “但现在很多事情都融合在一起了。”

articles.title: Extinct, long-legged grasshoppers walked on water alongside dinosaurs
articles.author: Jake Buehler

paras.en: Nearly 100 million years ago, spindly legged grasshoppers may have scooted across water like modern day water striders. The clues are in the fossilized insects’ legs and feet.
paras.zh: 近一亿年前，细长腿的蚱蜢可能像现代水黾一样在水面上快速移动。线索就在昆虫化石的腿和脚上。

paras.en: Special hairs and leaf-shaped leg adornments, exquisitely preserved in amber, suggest the insects — members of a newfound family of insects — could balance and slide around on surface tension, researchers report November 24 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The discovery suggests at least three insect groups evolved independently to move across water.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 11 月 24 日在《英国皇家学会学报 B》上报道称，琥珀中精美保存的特殊毛发和叶形腿部装饰表明，这些昆虫（新发现的昆虫家族的成员）可以在表面张力的作用下保持平衡和滑动。这一发现表明，至少三个昆虫群体独立进化以在水中移动。

paras.en: Paleontologist Chunpeng Xu and his colleagues first encountered the strange insects while studying a collection of 99-million-year-old amber. Frozen in time were three pieces of amber containing wingless grasshoppers with short bodies and incredibly long, skinny legs. Due to their unorthodox body shape, Xu didn’t recognize them as grasshoppers at first and thought they might be harvestmen or stick insects.
paras.zh: 古生物学家徐春鹏和他的同事在研究一批 9900 万年前的琥珀时首次遇到了这种奇怪的昆虫。三块琥珀被及时冻结，里面有无翼的蚱蜢，它们的身体很短，腿又长又瘦。由于体型奇特，徐一开始并没有认出它们是蝗虫，还以为它们可能是收割者或竹节虫。

paras.en: “I was genuinely amazed,” says Xu, of the Nanjing Institute of Geology and Paleontology in China. “They are among the most bizarre insects.”
paras.zh: “我真的很惊讶，”中国南京地质古生物研究所的徐说。 “它们是最奇怪的昆虫之一。”

paras.en: Under the microscope, two details stood out: Front legs with water repellant hairs and rear lower legs with leaf-shaped paddlelike structures. Estimates of the insects’ weight show they could have ridden on the water’s surface tension, with help from the repellant hairs on their legs and their spread-out footprint across the surface of the water. And the paddlelike lower legs would have propelled them forward.
paras.zh: 在显微镜下，有两个细节引人注目：前腿有防水毛，后小腿有叶状桨状结构。对昆虫重量的估计表明，在腿部的驱虫毛和遍布水面的足迹的帮助下，它们可以依靠水的表面张力来行走。桨状的小腿会推动它们前进。

paras.en: The researchers named the insects Hydrelcana zhangi, placing them in the new family Hydrelcanidae.
paras.zh: 研究人员将这种昆虫命名为“Hydrelcana zhangi”，将它们归入新的Hydrelcanidae科。

paras.en: “Walking on water is a pretty rare skill in nature,” Xu says. Until now, only two insect groups were known to have evolved to live on the water’s surface: water striders and their kin, and a similar looking but unrelated, long extinct family called Chresmodidae.
paras.zh: “在水上行走是自然界中一项非常罕见的技能，”徐说。 Until now, only two insect groups were known to have evolved to live on the water’s surface: water striders and their kin, and a similar looking but unrelated, long extinct family called Chresmodidae.

paras.en: The grasshoppers had a different gait from other water-walking insects. The common pond skater (Gerris lacustris), by comparison, rows with its middle limbs.
paras.zh: 蚱蜢的步态与其他水上行走昆虫不同。相比之下，常见的池塘溜冰者（Gerris lacustris）则用中肢划船。

paras.en: And whereas modern water-walking insects are predators and scavengers, the ancient grasshoppers were also probably herbivorous, given their mouthparts and lack of claws. The researchers found nine of them preserved in the same amber chunk, suggesting the insects may have gathered in large numbers to feed. It’s possibly the earliest record of such swarming behavior in grasshoppers or crickets, the team says.
paras.zh: 现代水中行走的昆虫是捕食者和食腐动物，而古代蚱蜢也可能是草食性的，因为它们有口器且没有爪子。研究人员发现其中九只保存在同一块琥珀中，这表明这些昆虫可能大量聚集在一起取食。研究小组表示，这可能是蚱蜢或蟋蟀此类集群行为的最早记录。

articles.title: Scientists Discover a Natural Sugar That May Help to Burn Visceral Fat
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: When it comes to weight loss, sometimes it can feel like it's you against the world.
paras.zh: 当谈到减肥时，有时你会感觉自己在对抗世界。

paras.en: As it happens, a multitude of invisible organisms living inside the gut have mysterious effects on the fat we carry.
paras.zh: 事实上，生活在肠道内的大量看不见的生物体对我们携带的脂肪有着神秘的影响。

paras.en: The better we can understand this hidden microbial relationship, the better we can stop weight gain from happening, and maybe even one day prevent obesity.
paras.zh: 我们越了解这种隐藏的微生物关系，我们就越能阻止体重增加，甚至有一天可以预防肥胖。

paras.en: In a new study in Cell Host & Microbe, scientists identified a bacterium that might prove helpful in the cause, called Clostridium immunis.
paras.zh: 在《细胞宿主与微生物》杂志上的一项新研究中，科学家们发现了一种可能有助于解决这一问题的细菌，称为免疫梭菌。

paras.en: Researchers had previously found that C. immunis can help protect mice against intestinal inflammation, but that's not all this particular microbe does.
paras.zh: 研究人员此前发现，免疫梭菌可以帮助保护小鼠免受肠道炎症的影响，但这并不是这种特殊微生物的全部作用。

paras.en: In an experiment with mice, animals given a single oral administration of the bacterium had 3 percent lower body weight in one week compared to control animals, and saw a 25 percent reduction in blood triglycerides.
paras.zh: 在一项小鼠实验中，与对照动物相比，单次口服该细菌的动物一周内体重降低了 3%，血液甘油三酯降低了 25%。

paras.en: Crucially, compared to control mice, the treated mice had about one-third less visceral fat – a type of fatty tissue that wraps around vital organs inside the abdominal cavity, which is linked to serious health risks if you have too much.
paras.zh: 至关重要的是，与对照组小鼠相比，接受治疗的小鼠的内脏脂肪减少了约三分之一，内脏脂肪是一种包裹腹腔内重要器官的脂肪组织，如果内脏脂肪过多，则会带来严重的健康风险。

paras.en: In a separate experiment, mice were fed a high-fat diet for 12 weeks. Control animals experienced 50 percent weight gain during the test, but mice treated with weekly doses of C. immunis showed 13 percent less weight gain that their control counterparts.
paras.zh: 在另一项实验中，小鼠被喂食高脂肪饮食 12 周。对照动物在测试期间体重增加了 50%，但每周接受免疫念珠菌治疗的小鼠的体重增加比对照小鼠少 13%。

paras.en: Subsequent experiments revealed the metabolic effects were due to a bioactive compound being released by the bacterium, which the researchers eventually discovered was a complex sugar molecule called an exopolysaccharide (EPS).
paras.zh: 随后的实验表明，代谢效应是由于细菌释放的生物活性化合物所致，研究人员最终发现这种化合物是一种称为胞外多糖（EPS）的复杂糖分子。

paras.en: When mice were given the EPS by itself, it produced the same weight-loss and fat-reduction effects in treated animals, suggesting it's the sugar, not the bacterium itself, that's responsible for the benefits seen.
paras.zh: 当小鼠单独服用 EPS 时，它在接受治疗的动物中产生了相同的减肥和减少脂肪的效果，这表明是糖，而不是细菌本身，才是所看到的好处的原因。

paras.en: The researchers found that the EPS molecule, which carries a chemical group called phosphocholine, reduces intestinal immune cells called ILC3 cells, suppressing their production of a signaling protein known as IL–22.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，携带磷酸胆碱化学基团的 EPS 分子会减少称为 ILC3 细胞的肠道免疫细胞，抑制其产生称为 IL-22 的信号蛋白。

paras.en: As IL–22 levels fall in the small intestine and visceral fat, more cells containing a protein called UCP1 appear in visceral fat.
paras.zh: 随着小肠和内脏脂肪中 IL-22 水平下降，内脏脂肪中会出现更多含有 UCP1 蛋白质的细胞。

paras.en: Because UCP1 is linked to thermogenesis – the process of burning energy to generate heat – this makes visceral fat more metabolically active, increasing the amount of energy the mice expend.
paras.zh: 因为 UCP1 与生热作用（燃烧能量产生热量的过程）有关，这使得内脏脂肪的代谢更加活跃，从而增加了小鼠消耗的能量。

paras.en: Remarkably, the mice achieved this without eating less or becoming more physically active.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，小鼠在没有减少饮食或增加体力活动的情况下实现了这一目标。

paras.en: "What surprised us was that this bacterial sugar did not work by reducing food intake or increasing activity," says first author and medical researcher Chin Yee Tan from Singapore General Hospital, who worked on the research at Duke-NUS Medical School in Singapore.
paras.zh: “令我们惊讶的是，这种细菌糖并不能通过减少食物摄入或增加活动来发挥作用，”新加坡中央医院的第一作者、医学研究员 Chin Yee Tan 说，他在新加坡杜克-新加坡国立大学医学院从事这项研究。

paras.en: "Instead, it changed how visceral fat used energy. That gives us a completely different way of thinking about how gut bacteria can influence metabolism."
paras.zh: “相反，它改变了内脏脂肪使用能量的方式。这让我们以完全不同的方式思考肠道细菌如何影响新陈代谢。”

paras.en: While there's a lot we still don't fully understand about how the process works, the EPS sugar produced by C. immunis appears to release a handbrake in the immune system that limits the energy-burning capacity of visceral fat, making the animals burn fat more effectively even when their eating and behavior were unchanged.
paras.zh: 虽然我们对这个过程的运作方式还有很多不完全了解，但免疫梭菌产生的 EPS 糖似乎会释放免疫系统的手刹，限制内脏脂肪的能量燃烧能力，使动物即使在饮食和行为不变的情况下也能更有效地燃烧脂肪。

paras.en: It's unknown for now whether the same kind of treatment would work safely in humans, as for now this has only been tested in mice, but there are some promising signs of related biological mechanisms at play in people.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚同样的治疗方法在人类中是否安全有效，因为目前这仅在小鼠身上进行了测试，但有一些有希望的迹象表明相关的生物机制在人类中发挥作用。

paras.en: As part of the study, the researchers investigated gut microbiome data from more than 4,000 individuals, finding that a bacterial gene involved in producing phosphocholine was less abundant in people with obesity. A separate analysis also linked lower abundance of the gene with higher blood triglyceride levels.
paras.zh: 作为该研究的一部分，研究人员调查了 4000 多人的肠道微生物组数据，发现肥胖人群中参与产生磷酸胆碱的细菌基因含量较低。一项单独的分析也将较低的基因丰度与较高的血液甘油三酯水平联系起来。

paras.en: Although it will fall to future studies to confirm the full implications, the researchers suggest their findings are consistent with the effects seen in mice being "generalizable to humans", which is huge if true.
paras.zh: 尽管完整的影响将由未来的研究来证实，但研究人员表示，他们的发现与在小鼠中观察到的“可推广到人类”的效果是一致的，如果属实的话，这是巨大的。

paras.en: "Our findings reveal how some gut bacteria are able to uniquely communicate with the human body – they generate distinctive molecules by chemically modifying the sugars they produce," says senior author and physician-scientist Neeraj Surana from Duke University.
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果揭示了一些肠道细菌如何能够与人体进行独特的交流——它们通过化学修饰它们产生的糖来产生独特的分子，”杜克大学的资深作者、医师兼科学家 Neeraj Surana 说。

paras.en: "This opens up a new perspective on how the microbiome can influence human metabolism and points to new opportunities for developing treatments for metabolic diseases."
paras.zh: “这为微生物组如何影响人类新陈代谢开辟了新的视角，并为开发代谢疾病的治疗方法提供了新的机会。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in Cell Host & Microbe.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《细胞宿主与微生物》杂志上。

articles.title: Slime Mold 'Intelligence' Might Just Be Physics After All
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Slime molds are famous for their apparent intelligence.
paras.zh: 粘菌因其明显的智力而闻名。

paras.en: The strange organisms aren't true molds, and aren't even fungi. They have no brain or nervous system, but have the ability to solve complex mazes, learn, and 'make decisions'. As they move, they leave a yellow tube along the path they take.
paras.zh: 这些奇怪的生物体并不是真正的霉菌，甚至都不是真菌。他们没有大脑或神经系统，但有能力解决复杂的迷宫、学习和“做出决定”。当他们移动时，他们会沿着所走的路径留下一条黄色的管子。

paras.en: A new mathematical study offers a physical explanation for why slime mold might solve problems the way it does – and it could have less to do with 'intelligence' and more to do with efficiency.
paras.zh: 一项新的数学研究为为什么粘菌能够以它的方式解决问题提供了物理解释——它可能与“智力”关系不大，而与效率关系更大。

paras.en: The yellow strands, or tubes, that trail the slime mold as it spreads actually carry fluid through its body.
paras.zh: 当粘菌扩散时，黄色的丝或管子实际上将液体输送到其体内。

paras.en: When the researchers modeled two tubes of different lengths joining the same points, they found that the combined cost of moving fluid and maintaining the tubes was lowest when only the shorter tube remained.
paras.zh: 当研究人员对连接相同点的两根不同长度的管道进行建模时，他们发现，当仅保留较短的管道时，移动流体和维护管道的综合成本最低。

paras.en: The research builds upon a maze experiment reported in Nature in 2000.
paras.zh: 该研究以 2000 年《自然》杂志报道的一项迷宫实验为基础。

paras.en: The slime mold, a species called Physarum polycephalum, was already spread through the passages of the maze when researchers placed food at two points.
paras.zh: 当研究人员将食物放在两个点时，粘菌（一种称为多头绒泡菌）已经在迷宫的通道中传播。

paras.en: As time passed, the mold withdrew from dead ends. The tube linking the two food sources followed the shortest route through the maze.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，模​​具从死胡同退出。连接两个食物源的管道沿着迷宫中最短路线走。

paras.en: Those tubes aren't fixed. Rhythmic contractions push fluid back and forth through the slime mold's body, and the tubes change in response.
paras.zh: 这些管子没有固定好。有节奏的收缩推动液体在粘菌体内来回流动，管道也会随之变化。

paras.en: An earlier mathematical model captured how this might work. In the model, tubes that carry more flow get wider, which makes it easier for fluid to pass through. Tubes that carry little flow shrink.
paras.zh: 一个早期的数学模型描述了它是如何工作的。在模型中，承载更多流量的管道会变得更宽，这使得流体更容易通过。流量较小的管子会收缩。

paras.en: Over time, that feedback can turn a network with several possible routes into one with a single main connection.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，这种反馈可以将具有多个可能路由的网络转变为具有单个主连接的网络。

paras.en: Ricard Solé and Jordi Pla-Mauri from Pompeu Fabra University in Spain, who led the new study, wanted to know why, so they looked at the problem in terms of energy.
paras.zh: 领导这项新研究的西班牙庞培法布拉大学的 Ricard Solé 和 Jordi Pla-Mauri 想知道其中的原因，因此他们从能源的角度来研究这个问题。

paras.en: They represented the two routes as the two sides of a ring, with both tubes linking the same pair of points.
paras.zh: 他们将两条路线表示为环的两侧，两条管道连接同一对点。

paras.en: First, they calculated how fluid would move through tubes of a given width. Then they looked at how the cost of running the network changed as the tubes widened or narrowed.
paras.zh: 首先，他们计算了流体如何通过给定宽度的管道流动。然后，他们研究了随着管道变宽或变窄，运行网络的成本如何变化。

paras.en: It comes down to a trade-off. Friction drains energy from fluid as it moves through a tube, and widening the tube reduces that resistance. But in the model, a wider tube also costs more to maintain.
paras.zh: 这归结为一个权衡。当流体穿过管道时，摩擦会消耗流体的能量，而加宽管道会减少阻力。但在该模型中，更宽的管子的维护成本也更高。

paras.en: The researchers worked out which tube widths gave the lowest total cost for both keeping the network in place and moving fluid through it.
paras.zh: 研究人员找出了哪种管宽可以使网络保持到位和使流体通过其中的总成本最低。

paras.en: When one side of the ring was longer, the cheapest option was to send all the flow through the shorter tube and let the longer one disappear.
paras.zh: 当环的一侧较长时，最便宜的选择是将所有流量通过较短的管子，让较长的管子消失。

paras.en: With two routes of equal length, any split of the flow could reach the same minimum cost, as long as the tube widths matched that split. In that case, how the flow ended up dividing depended on the condition of the tubes at the start.
paras.zh: 在两条长度相等的情况下，只要管宽度与该分流相匹配，任何分流的流量都可以达到相同的最低成本。在这种情况下，流体最终如何分开取决于管道开始时的状况。

paras.en: The researchers also tested the model on branching networks. A dead-end branch that carried no flow gradually vanished. But when the setup required fluid to reach several endpoints, the branches connecting them to the source stayed.
paras.zh: 研究人员还在分支网络上测试了该模型。一根没有流动的死枝渐渐消失了。但是，当设置需​​要流体到达多个端点时，将它们连接到源头的分支就会保留下来。

paras.en: Because the model makes specific predictions, it can be tested against real slime mold. In the ring setup, for example, researchers could keep both routes the same length, vary the starting widths, and see whether those differences predict how the flow ends up being shared.
paras.zh: 由于该模型会做出具体的预测，因此可以针对真实的粘菌进行测试。例如，在环形设置中，研究人员可以保持两条路线相同的长度，改变起始宽度，并看看这些差异是否可以预测流量最终如何共享。

paras.en: There are limits, though. People design the maze and decide where the food goes, so the layout already defines the problem the slime mold appears to solve. And the model only kicks in once the organism has formed a connected network in that layout.
paras.zh: 但也有限制。人们设计迷宫并决定食物的去向，因此布局已经定义了粘菌似乎要解决的问题。只有当生物体在该布局中形成一个连接的网络时，该模型才会生效。

paras.en: It doesn't explain how a slime mold explores new ground or finds food in the first place. It also doesn't cover other behaviors seen in different experiments, including learning and habituation – a weakening response to a repeated stimulus.
paras.zh: 它并没有解释粘菌最初是如何探索新的土地或寻找食物的。它还没有涵盖不同实验中看到的其他行为，包括学习和习惯——对重复刺激的减弱反应。

paras.en: What it does explain is how a web that already spans several passages can end up with a single tube linking the food sources. And it hints that the answer might have less to do with thinking, and more to do with not wasting energy.
paras.zh: 它所解释的是，已经跨越多个通道的网如何最终成为连接食物源的单个管子。它暗示答案可能与思考关系不大，而与不浪费精力关系更大。

paras.en: The research has been published in Journal of the Royal Society Interface.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《皇家学会界面杂志》上。

articles.title: There Is One Predator That Terrifies Bears And Mountain Lions Alike
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: The wilds of North America can be a hazardous place.
paras.zh: 北美的荒野可能是一个危险的地方。

paras.en: It's there that some of the most intimidating predators make their home – black and brown bears that could eviscerate a person with one swipe of a mighty paw, and mountain lions that stalk almost silently on padded feet.
paras.zh: 一些最令人生畏的掠食者在这里安家——黑熊和棕熊可以用强大的爪子一击就将人掏出内脏，而山狮则用带衬垫的脚几乎无声无息地潜行。

paras.en: Many hikers will gird themselves against the possibility of an attack from one of these feared beasts.
paras.zh: 许多徒步旅行者都会做好准备，以防这些可怕的野兽袭击的可能性。

paras.en: But, as two recent papers explain, there's an animal out there that even the most formidable predators will try to avoid.
paras.zh: 但是，正如最近的两篇论文所解释的那样，有一种动物即使是最强大的掠食者也会试图避开。

paras.en: In fact, attacks by these animals are so uncommon that, in North America, people are far more likely to be struck by lightning.
paras.zh: 事实上，这些动物的袭击非常罕见，以至于在北美，人们被闪电击中的可能性要大得多。

paras.en: The research suggests one reason why: Bears and mountain lions go to remarkable lengths to stay away from humans whenever they can.
paras.zh: 这项研究提出了一个原因：熊和山狮会尽可能地远离人类。

paras.en: "These discoveries change the narrative about human-carnivore conflict," writes Yale University ecologist Oswald Schmitz in a Current Biology dispatch tying together two studies, one on bears and the other on mountain lions.
paras.zh: “这些发现改变了关于人类与肉食动物冲突的叙述，”耶鲁大学生态学家奥斯瓦尔德·施密茨在《当代生物学》快报中写道，该快报将两项研究结合在一起，一项是关于熊的，另一项是关于山狮的。

paras.en: In North America, brown, or grizzly, bears (Ursus arctos) attack, on average, around 11.4 humans per year.
paras.zh: 在北美，棕熊（Ursus arctos）平均每年攻击约 11.4 人。

paras.en: Mountain lions (Puma concolor) attack just 4 to 6 people per year, and the rate of black bear (Ursus americanus) attacks is unknown, but just 63 human fatalities due to black bear attacks were documented between 1900 and 2009.
paras.zh: 山狮 (Puma concolor) 每年仅攻击 4 至 6 人，黑熊 (Ursus americanus) 的攻击率尚不清楚，但 1900 年至 2009 年间仅记录了 63 人因黑熊攻击而死亡。

paras.en: By contrast, across the US and Canada, around 580 people are struck by lightning every year.
paras.zh: 相比之下，在美国和加拿大，每年约有 580 人被闪电击中。

paras.en: Looking purely at the numbers, lightning strikes outnumber brown bear attacks by roughly 50 to 1 (although, of course, the actual risk depends on other factors such as where you live and how much time you spend in bear-filled woods).
paras.zh: 单纯从数字来看，闪电袭击与棕熊袭击的数量大约为 50 比 1（当然，实际风险取决于其他因素，例如您居住的地方以及您在熊出没的树林中度过的时间）。

paras.en: According to the two studies, the answer is that these animals don't simply react to humans showing up. Instead, they actively change their behaviors to avoid us.
paras.zh: 根据这两项研究，答案是这些动物不会简单地对人类的出现做出反应。相反，他们主动改变自己的行为来避开我们。

paras.en: In a study led by wildlife biologist Philip Manlick of the USDA Forest Service, researchers studied bears and other predators feeding along salmon streams in southeast Alaska.
paras.zh: 在美国农业部林务局野生动物生物学家菲利普·曼利克领导的一项研究中，研究人员研究了在阿拉斯加东南部沿鲑鱼溪流捕食的熊和其他食肉动物。

paras.en: They placed salmon by the streams, and motion-triggered speakers played recordings of either gull calls, off-road vehicles, or human voices whenever an animal approached. Cameras recorded what happened next.
paras.zh: 他们将鲑鱼放在溪边，每当有动物靠近时，动作触发扬声器就会播放海鸥叫声、越野车或人声的录音。摄像机记录了接下来发生的事情。

paras.en: The animals – bears, bald eagles, and ravens – were twice as likely to beat a hasty retreat when they heard vehicle sounds compared to the gull sounds.
paras.zh: 熊、秃鹰和乌鸦等动物在听到车辆声音时匆忙撤退的可能性是听到海鸥声音时的两倍。

paras.en: They were almost 10 times more likely to flee from the sound of human voices.
paras.zh: 他们逃离人类声音的可能性几乎高出十倍。

paras.en: This has implications far beyond bear-human interactions.
paras.zh: 这所产生的影响远远超出了熊与人类的互动范围。

paras.en: A 2024 study in British Columbia used chemical signatures in 226 hair samples from grizzly bears across 22 salmon rivers to estimate how much salmon each bear ate.
paras.zh: 2024 年，不列颠哥伦比亚省的一项研究使用了 22 条鲑鱼河流中灰熊的 226 个毛发样本中的化学特征来估计每只熊吃了多少鲑鱼。

paras.en: Where riverside areas had more human disturbance – mostly from industry – the researchers found bears' salmon consumption strongly decreased (by up to 59 percent in females).
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，在人类干扰较多的河滨地区（主要来自工业），熊的鲑鱼消费量大幅下降（雌性熊的鲑鱼消费量下降高达 59%）。

paras.en: Bears take the salmon they catch into nearby forests, leaving behind decaying remnants that help fertilize the ecosystem. Disrupting that nutrient transport has knock-on effects on other ecosystem processes.
paras.zh: 熊将捕获的鲑鱼带到附近的森林，留下腐烂的残余物，帮助肥沃生态系统。破坏养分运输会对其他生态系统过程产生连锁反应。

paras.en: At sites playing human sounds, Manlick and colleagues reported that animals fed more at night, and bears' overall effect on decomposition in the forest was weaker than at the quiet control sites.
paras.zh: 曼利克和同事报告说，在播放人类声音的地点，动物在夜间进食更多，而且熊对森林分解的总体影响比安静的对照地点要弱。

paras.en: The mountain lion paper, led by environmental scientist John Morgan of the University of California, Santa Cruz, told a similar tale.
paras.zh: 由加州大学圣克鲁斯分校环境科学家约翰·摩根领导的山狮论文也讲述了类似的故事。

paras.en: The researchers analyzed six years of GPS data collected from 36 tagged wild mountain lions in the Santa Cruz Mountains.
paras.zh: 研究人员分析了从圣克鲁斯山脉 36 只标记的野生美洲狮收集的六年 GPS 数据。

paras.en: They mapped this data against data from the GPS fitness-tracking app Strava, which showed where and when people were hiking, biking, and using trails.
paras.zh: 他们将这些数据与 GPS 健身追踪应用程序 Strava 的数据进行了映射，该应用程序显示了人们徒步旅行、骑自行车和使用小径的地点和时间。

paras.en: The mountain lions didn't just respond to the presence of humans.
paras.zh: 山狮不仅仅对人类的存在做出反应。

paras.en: Rather, they seemed to anticipate where and when human activity was likely to be heavy, and proactively avoided those places at those times.
paras.zh: 相反，它们似乎预见到了人类活动可能在何时何地变得频繁，并在那时主动避开了这些地方。

paras.en: Even when mountain lions lived in areas with lots of human activity, though, they were not more likely to be involved in conflicts, including sightings, attacks on pets or livestock, and, rarely, attacks on people.
paras.zh: 然而，即使山狮生活在人类活动频繁的地区，它们也不太可能卷入冲突，包括目击事件、攻击宠物或牲畜，以及在极少数情况下攻击人类。

paras.en: Conflict was better explained simply by more frequent encounters between people and mountain lions.
paras.zh: 冲突可以通过人与美洲狮之间更频繁的接触来更好地解释。

paras.en: Taken together, the two studies suggest that the animals take actions that indicate they perceive humans as a significant threat.
paras.zh: 总的来说，这两项研究表明，动物采取的行动表明它们将人类视为重大威胁。

paras.en: Bears abandon their feeding opportunities. Mountain lions plan their movements around predictable human routines.
paras.zh: 熊放弃了进食机会。山狮根据可预测的人类惯例来计划它们的行动。

paras.en: They're already doing a lot of the heavy lifting that prevents dangerous encounters with our own species.
paras.zh: 他们已经做了很多繁重的工作，以防止与我们自己的物种发生危险的遭遇。

paras.en: For our end of the bargain, the mountain lion study suggests, we can try to avoid forcing them into situations where their avoidance strategies fail.
paras.zh: 山狮研究表明，为了讨价还价，我们可以尽量避免迫使它们陷入回避策略失败的境地。

paras.en: In February 2026, California's Fish and Game Commission voted to list mountain lion populations along the Central Coast and in Southern California, including those in the Santa Cruz Mountains, as threatened under the state's Endangered Species Act.
paras.zh: 2026 年 2 月，加州渔猎委员会投票将中央海岸和南加州（包括圣克鲁斯山脉的山狮）种群列为该州《濒危物种法》所威胁的种群。

paras.en: "Mountain lions in the Santa Cruz Mountains are at increased risk of extinction, due to a lack of genetic diversity and habitat connectivity," Morgan explains.
paras.zh: 摩根解释说：“由于缺乏遗传多样性和栖息地连通性，圣克鲁斯山脉的美洲狮面临着更大的灭绝风险。”

paras.en: Related: A Wild Puma Was Caught on Camera Hunting in an Unexpected Place
paras.zh: 相关：一只野生美洲狮被摄像机拍到在一个意想不到的地方狩猎

paras.en: The popular image of the relationship between humans and carnivorous predators is that the predator is the aggressor, and the human is the helpless prey that stands to lose the most from an encounter.
paras.zh: 关于人类和肉食性掠食者之间关系的流行印象是，掠食者是侵略者，而人类是无助的猎物，在遭遇中损失最大。

paras.en: In reality, Schmitz argues, humans have not just the power but the responsibility to do all that we can to keep those animals safe.
paras.zh: 施密茨认为，事实上，人类不仅有权力，而且有责任尽一切努力保护这些动物的安全。

paras.en: "By being cognizant of how they shape the landscape of fear experienced by carnivores and their prey species, humans can proactively adjust their behavior and spatial use of landscapes in ways that can transform the human-carnivore relationship from one of conflict to one of coexistence," he writes.
paras.zh: 他写道：“通过认识到它们如何塑造食肉动物及其猎物所经历的恐惧景观，人类可以主动调整自己的行为和对景观的空间利用，从而将人与食肉动物的关系从冲突关系转变为共存关系。”

paras.en: "And thereby rebalance the attendant cascading effects that human fear effects have on wildlife communities and ecosystems."
paras.zh: “从而重新平衡人类恐惧对野生动物群落和生态系统产生的连锁效应。”

paras.en: All three papers have been published in Current Biology.
paras.zh: 所有三篇论文均发表在《当代生物学》上。

paras.en: You can read the bear paper here, the mountain lion paper here, and Schmitz's dispatch here.
paras.zh: 您可以在这里阅读熊报、山狮报和施密茨的快报。

articles.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

paras.en: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat
paras.zh: 科学家发现了一种普通抗抑郁药难以治疗的新型抑郁症

paras.en: Experts hope discovery will lead to alternative and more targeted behavioural and medical treatments, notably in young people in the early stages of these disorders.
paras.zh: 专家希望这一发现将带来替代性的、更有针对性的行为和医学治疗，特别是对于处于这些疾病早期阶段的年轻人。

paras.en: Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. Traditional antidepressants often work less effectively for these individuals, potentially explaining why some people struggle to find relief.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现了一种新的抑郁症亚型，可能影响近四分之一的重度、复发性或持续性抑郁症患者。它被称为“昼夜节律抑制”，与人体的生物钟有关，并与夜猫子倾向、过度睡眠、持续疲惫和更严重的症状有关。传统的抗抑郁药物通常对这些人效果较差，这可能解释了为什么有些人难以寻求缓解。

paras.en: A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.
paras.zh: 一种新发现的抑郁症可能有助于解释为什么有些人很难从常用的抗抑郁药中找到缓解方法。 Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

paras.en: The discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, showed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.
paras.zh: 这一发现是对 10,000 多名澳大利亚抑郁症患者的临床和遗传信息进行分析得出的。这项研究主要针对患有严重、复发或持续性抑郁症的人，近四分之一的参与者表现出这种新发现的亚型的特征。

paras.en: Circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.
paras.zh: 昼夜节律抑制与人体的 24 小时生物钟有关，它有助于调节我们何时感到清醒和何时感到困倦。患有这种抑郁症的人往往对常见的基于血清素的抗抑郁药反应较差。然而，针对参与控制昼夜节律的大脑回路的治疗，包括褪黑激素、针对褪黑激素的抗抑郁药和光疗法，可能会提供更有效的选择。

paras.en: Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.
paras.zh: 发表在《英国精神病学杂志》上的研究结果揭示了与这种亚型相关的遗传因素，并为为什么广泛使用的药物如 SSRIs（选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂）对某些患者效果较差提供了可能的解释。

paras.en: A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied
paras.zh: 一种隐藏的抑郁症影响了近四分之一的研究患者

paras.en: To investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.
paras.zh: 为了调查不同形式抑郁症之间的生物学差异，研究人员检查了通过全国性澳大利亚抑郁症遗传学研究收集的信息。他们的分析包括 10,000 多名抑郁症患者的临床病史和遗传数据。

paras.en: The researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现近 25% 的人（2,604 名参与者）患有昼夜节律抑郁症。一些可识别的模式将这些人与其他抑郁症患者区分开来。

paras.en: Those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.
paras.zh: 具有昼夜节律亚型的人更有可能经历抑郁症的季节性变化，在抑郁时睡眠时间更长，尽管在床上的时间更长，但醒来时仍感到精疲力竭。他们也更有可能是夜猫子，这意味着他们自然更喜欢熬夜并在一天中晚些时候起床。

paras.en: The differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.
paras.zh: 差异不仅限于睡眠模式。这些人的抑郁症通常在生命早期就开始出现，而且他们的症状往往更严重（例如躁狂和更高程度的自杀念头）。基因分析还显示，人们更容易患炎症和心血管健康问题，以及包括注意力缺陷多动症（ADHD）在内的主要神经发育障碍。

paras.en: First author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:
paras.zh: 第一作者、悉尼大学大脑与思维中心的 Emiliana Tonini 博士说：

paras.en: "Our research has identified circadian depression as a new subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.
paras.zh: “我们的研究已将昼夜节律抑郁症确定为一种新的亚型，在我们的研究中，约四分之一的人患有严重、复发或持续性抑郁症。

paras.en: "Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them."
paras.zh: “抑郁症不是一种统一的疾病，了解不同亚型的特征意味着我们可以让人们尽早获得对他们最有效的治疗。”

paras.en: Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective
paras.zh: 为什么普通的抗抑郁药效果可能较差

paras.en: One of the most important implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.
paras.zh: 这一发现最重要的意义之一涉及如何治疗抑郁症。

paras.en: Medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.
paras.zh: SSRI 和 SNRI（血清素和去甲肾上腺素再摄取抑制剂）等药物通常是为诊断为抑郁症的患者提供的首选治疗方法。这些药物通过影响大脑中有助于调节情绪的化学信使发挥作用。

paras.en: However, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.
paras.zh: 然而，研究人员发现这些药物对于昼夜节律抑郁症患者的效果往往较差。患有这种亚型的人也会经历更多的副作用，这表明传统的抗抑郁药可能不是适合每个人的最佳初始方法。

paras.en: Because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.
paras.zh: 由于昼夜节律抑制与人体的内部时钟密切相关，因此旨在影响该时钟的疗法可能特别有用。例如，光疗法利用受控的强光照射来帮助调节生物节律。褪黑激素是一种与身体何时准备睡眠有关的激素，而针对褪黑激素途径的抗抑郁药也可能是相关的治疗选择。

paras.en: Co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:
paras.zh: 大脑与思维中心的共同资深作者雅各布·克劳斯博士解释说：

paras.en: "Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.
paras.zh: “由于昼夜节律抑郁与人们的体内生物钟有关，因此针对昼夜节律的治疗，例如光疗和褪黑激素，可能更相关，临床医生应该更早地对患有这种表现的人进行这些治疗。

paras.en: "For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is important to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances."
paras.zh: “对于那些发现抗抑郁药对他们不起作用的人来说，向您的临床医生咨询有关您个人情况的建议非常重要。”

paras.en: A New Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People
paras.zh: 一种新方法可以改善年轻人的抑郁症治疗

paras.en: Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially important for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.
paras.zh: 尽早认识昼夜节律抑郁症对于年轻患者尤其重要，否则他们可能会花费宝贵的时间尝试不太适合其特定形式抑郁症的药物。

paras.en: Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.
paras.zh: 大脑与思维中心联合主任、临床精神病学家 Ian Hickie 教授警告说，未能识别年轻人的这种亚型可能会导致早期治疗不成功和不必要的副作用。

paras.en: The findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.
paras.zh: 研究结果强调了认识到抑郁症不是单一、统一的病症的重要性。不同的生物学机制可能会导致类似的症状，这意味着对一个人有效的治疗可能对另一个人提供的益处要少得多。

paras.en: By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.
paras.zh: 通过识别抑郁症与昼夜节律密切相关的患者，临床医生也许能够更早地提供更有针对性的治疗，而不是依赖于为每个人提供相同的初始药物治疗方法。

paras.en: "We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.
paras.zh: “我们真的希望年轻人在病程早期接受最合适的治疗。

paras.en: "Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition."
paras.zh: “大多数年轻人将首先接受 SSRIs，但至少有四分之一的年轻人有更好的以昼夜节律为中心的医疗和行为选择来帮助治疗和管理他们的病情。”

paras.zh: 材料由悉尼大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: A black hole the size of an atom could destroy an entire star

paras.en: A black hole the size of an atom could destroy an entire star
paras.zh: 一个原子大小的黑洞可以摧毁整个恒星

paras.en: MIT scientists have discovered that tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang could slowly devour stars from within, eventually triggering spectacular explosions visible across galaxies. Detecting these unusual cosmic events could reveal the existence of primordial black holes and help solve the mystery of dark matter.
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院的科学家发现，大爆炸留下的微小黑洞可以慢慢地从内部吞噬恒星，最终引发整个星系可见的壮观爆炸。探测这些不寻常的宇宙事件可以揭示原始黑洞的存在，并有助于解开暗物质之谜。

paras.en: Some of the smallest black holes ever proposed may be capable of destroying entire stars from the inside. Scientists believe these mysterious objects, known as primordial black holes, could have formed during the first fraction of a second after the Big Bang, when extremely dense regions of matter collapsed under their own gravity. If they exist, these ancient remnants could also account for a substantial portion of dark matter, the invisible material that makes up most of the matter in the universe.
paras.zh: 一些有史以来最小的黑洞可能能够从内部摧毁整个恒星。科学家认为，这些被称为太初黑洞的神秘物体可能是在大爆炸后的最初几分之一秒内形成的，当时极其致密的物质区域在自身重力作用下坍缩了。如果它们存在，这些古老的遗迹也可以解释暗物质的很大一部分，暗物质是构成宇宙中大部分物质的不可见物质。

paras.en: Researchers at MIT and other institutions have now identified a possible way to find them. Using theoretical calculations and computer simulations in three dimensions, the team investigated what would happen if a primordial black hole became trapped inside a star similar to our Sun.
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院和其他机构的研究人员现已找到一种可能的方法来找到它们。研究小组利用三维理论计算和计算机模拟，研究了如果原始黑洞被困在类似于太阳的恒星内会发生什么。

paras.en: Their study, published in The Astrophysical Journal, describes a remarkable possibility. A black hole no larger than an atom, but carrying the mass of an asteroid, could gradually sink toward the center of a star and begin consuming it from within.
paras.zh: 他们的研究发表在《天体物理学杂志》上，描述了一种非凡的可能性。一个不大于原子但具有小行星质量的黑洞可能会逐渐沉向恒星中心并开始从内部吞噬它。

paras.en: If the star rotates rapidly enough, material falling toward the black hole would eventually form a spinning disk around it. That development could set the stage for a catastrophic explosion.
paras.zh: 如果恒星旋转得足够快，落向黑洞的物质最终会在其周围形成一个旋转的圆盘。这种发展可能为灾难性的爆炸埋下伏笔。

paras.en: "Once the disk forms, this is essentially a death sentence for the star," says lead author Ore Gottlieb, an assistant professor of physics at MIT.
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院物理学助理教授、主要作者奥雷·戈特利布（Ore Gottlieb）说：“一旦圆盘形成，这基本上就等于对恒星宣判了死刑。”

paras.en: The interaction between the black hole and the surrounding disk could produce enormous jets of matter that punch through the star and cause it to explode within seconds. Researchers predict that the resulting outburst would emit intense blue and ultraviolet light, along with X-rays and gamma rays, potentially making it visible to telescopes already in operation.
paras.zh: 黑洞与周围圆盘之间的相互作用可能会产生巨大的物质射流，穿过恒星并导致其在几秒钟内爆炸。研究人员预测，由此产生的爆发将发出强烈的蓝色和紫外线，以及X射线和伽马射线，可能使已经运行的望远镜看到它。

paras.en: "There is hope for us to probe primordial black holes through interactions with stars," Gottlieb says. "We expect this to be visible, and it's something we should look into."
paras.zh: “我们有希望通过与恒星的相互作用来探测太初黑洞，”戈特利布说。 “我们希望这是可见的，这是我们应该调查的事情。”

paras.en: The research team also included Matteo Cantiello of the Flatiron Institute, Cameron Norton and Matthew Kleban of New York University, and Ken Van Tilburg of Stanford University.
paras.zh: 研究小组还包括熨斗研究所的马泰奥·坎蒂洛、纽约大学的卡梅伦·诺顿和马修·克莱班以及斯坦福大学的肯·范·蒂尔堡。

paras.en: Ancient Black Holes That May Have Survived the Big Bang
paras.zh: 可能在大爆炸中幸存下来的古代黑洞

paras.en: Not every primordial black hole formed in the early universe would still exist today. According to a theory developed by physicist Stephen Hawking, black holes gradually lose energy through a quantum process called Hawking radiation. Over immense periods of time, this process causes them to shrink, and the smallest primordial black holes would already have evaporated completely.
paras.zh: 并非早期宇宙中形成的所有原始黑洞今天仍然存在。根据物理学家斯蒂芬·霍金提出的理论，黑洞通过称为霍金辐射的量子过程逐渐失去能量。在很长一段时间内，这个过程导致它们收缩，最小的原初黑洞已经完全蒸发了。

paras.en: Heavier primordial black holes, however, could have survived to the present day. Some might be approximately the size of an atom while containing as much mass as an asteroid (or about a millionth of the mass of the Earth).
paras.zh: 然而，较重的原始黑洞可能存活至今。有些可能大约有原子大小，但质量与小行星相当（或约为地球质量的百万分之一）。

paras.en: These extraordinary objects raise an intriguing question. If they are still scattered throughout the universe, what would happen when one encounters a star? More importantly, could the resulting interaction provide the evidence needed to establish that primordial black holes actually exist?
paras.zh: 这些非凡的物体提出了一个有趣的问题。如果它们仍然分散在宇宙各处，当遇到一颗恒星时会发生什么？更重要的是，由此产生的相互作用能否提供证明原始黑洞确实存在所需的证据？

paras.en: To investigate, Gottlieb and his colleagues combined mathematical calculations with numerical simulations incorporating general relativity, fluid dynamics, stellar evolution, and particle physics. Their goal was to understand how a primordial black hole could become trapped by a star and what would happen afterward.
paras.zh: 为了进行研究，戈特利布和他的同事将数学计算与数值模拟相结合，其中包括广义相对论、流体动力学、恒星演化和粒子物理学。他们的目标是了解原始黑洞如何被恒星捕获以及之后会发生什么。

paras.en: How a Tiny Black Hole Could Become Trapped Inside a Star
paras.zh: 微小黑洞如何被困在恒星内部

paras.en: The researchers found that a star acting alone generally could not capture a primordial black hole passing nearby. Its gravitational attraction would be insufficient to keep the black hole from escaping.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，单独行动的恒星通常无法捕获经过附近的原始黑洞。它的引力不足以阻止黑洞逃逸。

paras.en: The situation changes when another object is involved. A companion star or planet could alter the gravitational interaction enough to allow the primordial black hole to become trapped.
paras.zh: 当涉及另一个对象时，情况就会发生变化。伴星或行星可能会改变引力相互作用，足以让原始黑洞被困住。

paras.en: In this arrangement involving three objects, the black hole could repeatedly travel through the star. Each passage would create friction as it moved through stellar material, gradually draining energy from its orbit and drawing it closer to the star's center.
paras.zh: 在涉及三个物体的这种排列中，黑洞可以反复穿过恒星。当它穿过恒星物质时，每次通过都会产生摩擦，逐渐耗尽其轨道的能量并将其拉近恒星中心。

paras.en: The process could take thousands or even millions of years. Although that sounds extraordinarily slow, it is relatively brief compared with the age of the universe.
paras.zh: 这个过程可能需要数千年甚至数百万年。虽然这听起来异常缓慢，但与宇宙的年龄相比却相对短暂。

paras.en: Eventually, the black hole would settle into the star's core, where it could begin feeding on the surrounding material.
paras.zh: 最终，黑洞将进入恒星的核心，在那里它可以开始以周围的物质为食。

paras.en: "Then, this is where the action begins," Gottlieb says.
paras.zh: “然后，这就是行动开始的地方，”戈特利布说。

paras.en: A Black Hole Could Slowly Consume a Star From Within
paras.zh: 黑洞可能会慢慢地从内部吞噬一颗恒星

paras.en: Once the primordial black hole reaches the stellar core, its growth depends partly on what happens to the energy generated as gas falls toward it. Some of that energy can heat the surrounding material, potentially slowing the rate at which additional gas falls inward.
paras.zh: 一旦原始黑洞到达恒星核心，它的增长部分取决于气体落向它时产生的能量的变化。其中一些能量可以加热周围的材料，可能会减慢额外气体向内落下的速度。

paras.en: The team's simulations indicate that most of the energy would instead disappear into the black hole. This would allow it to accumulate matter more rapidly than earlier estimates suggested.
paras.zh: 该团队的模拟表明，大部分能量会消失在黑洞中。这将使其能够比之前估计的更快地积累物质。

paras.en: Over several million years, the growing black hole could consume approximately 1 percent of the star's total mass. At that stage, its fate would depend heavily on how quickly the star rotates.
paras.zh: 在几百万年的时间里，不断增长的黑洞可能会消耗恒星总质量的大约 1%。在那个阶段，它的命运将在很大程度上取决于恒星自转的速度。

paras.en: If the star spins fast enough, gas would no longer be able to plunge directly into the black hole. Instead, the material would gather into a rotating disk around the black hole, which would by then have grown to several meters in size.
paras.zh: 如果恒星旋转得足够快，气体将不再能够直接冲入黑洞。相反，这些物质会聚集成黑洞周围的旋转圆盘，届时该圆盘的大小将达到几米。

paras.en: "Inside the star, you have a black hole with a disk," Gottlieb says. "The black hole is also spinning, and it's twisting space and time."
paras.zh: “在恒星内部，有一个带有圆盘的黑洞，”戈特利布说。 “黑洞也在旋转，它扭曲着空间和时间。”

paras.en: As the disk continues feeding the black hole, the extreme rotation twists the magnetic field threading the surrounding material. This process could generate exceptionally powerful jets that shoot outward from the black hole's poles.
paras.zh: 当圆盘继续向黑洞提供能量时，极端的旋转扭曲了穿过周围材料的磁场。这个过程可能会产生异常强大的喷流，从黑洞的两极向外喷射。

paras.en: "This twisted magnetic field will power very strong electromagnetic jets from the poles of the black hole," Gottlieb explains. "And these jets will just explode the star, within a few dozen seconds. It's very fast. Once you have a disk, you are done."
paras.zh: 戈特利布解释说：“这种扭曲的磁场将为来自黑洞两极的非常强的电磁射流提供动力。” “这些喷射器将在几十秒内爆炸恒星。速度非常快。一旦你有了圆盘，你就完成了。”

paras.en: What began as a tiny black hole hidden inside an otherwise ordinary star could therefore end in a violent explosion, with the star's destruction unfolding in a matter of seconds once the critical conditions are reached.
paras.zh: 因此，最初隐藏在一颗普通恒星内部的微小黑洞可能会以剧烈爆炸告终，一旦达到临界条件，恒星的毁灭将在几秒钟内展开。

paras.en: Exploding Stars Could Reveal Primordial Black Holes and Dark Matter
paras.zh: 爆炸的恒星可能揭示原始黑洞和暗物质

paras.en: The researchers also calculated what these unusual explosions might look like to astronomers, estimating how their brightness and color would change across different wavelengths of light.
paras.zh: 研究人员还计算了这些不寻常的爆炸在天文学家看来可能是什么样子，估计它们的亮度和颜色在不同波长的光下会如何变化。

paras.en: Their models predict a recognizable sequence of emissions, beginning with high-energy radiation and progressing through other parts of the electromagnetic spectrum as the explosion evolves. The initial outburst could include intense blue and ultraviolet light, along with gamma rays and X-rays.
paras.zh: 他们的模型预测了一系列可识别的发射序列，从高能辐射开始，随着爆炸的发展，逐渐穿过电磁波谱的其他部分。最初的爆发可能包括强烈的蓝光和紫外线，以及伽马射线和 X 射线。

paras.en: "We would initially detect some X-rays and gamma rays, then over time optical and infrared emissions, and later on radio emissions," Gottlieb says. "This is something we could potentially detect, if it's not happening too far from us. It could be many galaxies away, not just in our backyard."
paras.zh: “我们最初会检测到一些 X 射线和伽马射线，然后随着时间的推移检测光学和红外发射，最后检测无线电发射，”戈特利布说。 “如果它不是发生在离我们太远的地方，我们就有可能探测到它。它可能在许多星系之外，而不仅仅是在我们的后院。”

paras.en: Such signals could be detectable with existing astronomical instruments, potentially allowing researchers to search for primordial black holes far beyond the Milky Way.
paras.zh: 现有的天文仪器可以检测到此类信号，这可能使研究人员能够寻找远离银河系的原始黑洞。

paras.en: However, identifying one would not be straightforward. Other cosmic events can generate similar flashes of radiation, so an unusual explosion alone would not establish that a primordial black hole was responsible.
paras.zh: 然而，识别一个人并不容易。其他宇宙事件也能产生类似的辐射闪光，因此仅凭一次不寻常的爆炸并不能证明原始黑洞是造成这种现象的原因。

paras.en: Astronomers would need to examine additional evidence, including the characteristics of the exploding star. One especially revealing clue would be an explosion involving a star that would not ordinarily be expected to meet such a violent end.
paras.zh: 天文学家需要检查更多证据，包括爆炸恒星的特征。一个特别能说明问题的线索是，一颗恒星发生爆炸，而通常情况下，人们不会期望它会遭遇如此暴力的结局。

paras.en: "For instance, if the star is a certain mass that is not supposed to explode, it must be something that is happening inside that is a sort of parasite that is consuming the star from the inside," Gottlieb says. "The broader impact is that we can now place constraints on primordial black holes, and their contributions to dark matter, using observations."
paras.zh: 戈特利布说：“例如，如果恒星具有一定的质量，不应该爆炸，那么内部一定发生了某种寄生虫，从内部吞噬了恒星。” “更广泛的影响是，我们现在可以通过观测来限制原始黑洞及其对暗物质的贡献。”

paras.en: Even if no convincing examples are found, the search could help scientists determine how common primordial black holes might be and how much dark matter they could account for.
paras.zh: 即使没有找到令人信服的例子，这项研究也可以帮助科学家确定原始黑洞的普遍程度以及它们可以解释多少暗物质。

paras.en: For now, primordial black holes remain hypothetical. But the new research offers astronomers a possible observational signature to pursue, connecting the spectacular destruction of stars with objects that may have existed since the universe's earliest moments.
paras.zh: 目前，原始黑洞仍然是假设的。但这项新研究为天文学家提供了一个可能的观测特征，将恒星的壮观毁灭与自宇宙诞生之初就可能存在的物体联系起来。

paras.en: The research received partial support from the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science Advanced Scientific Computing Research Program and the National Science Foundation.
paras.zh: 该研究得到了美国能源部科学办公室高级科学计算研究计划和国家科学基金会的部分支持。

paras.en: Materials provided by Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Original written by Jennifer Chu. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由麻省理工学院提供。原创作者：朱珍妮。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Ore Gottlieb, Matteo Cantiello, Cameron Norton, Ken Van Tilburg, Matthew Kleban. The Life and Death of Stars that Capture Primordial Black Holes. The Astrophysical Journal, 2026; 1012 (1): 157 DOI: 10.3847/1538-4357/aeb7e1
paras.zh: - 奥雷·戈特利布、马泰奥·坎蒂洛、卡梅伦·诺顿、肯·范·蒂尔堡、马修·克莱班。捕获原始黑洞的恒星的生与死。天体物理学杂志，2026； 1012 (1): 157 DOI: 10.3847/1538-4357/aeb7e1

articles.title: New nose drops restore youthful memory and fight Alzheimer’s in aging mice

paras.en: New nose drops restore youthful memory and fight Alzheimerâs in aging mice
paras.zh: 新的滴鼻剂可恢复年轻记忆并对抗衰老小鼠的阿尔茨海默病

paras.en: A revolutionary new nasal treatment has restored youthful learning and memory performance in aging mice while preventing severe cognitive decline in mice with Alzheimerâs-like disease. Developed using technology similar to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, the nose drops stimulate production of a brain-protecting protein that strengthens neurons and supports memory. Remarkably, the treatment preserved brain function without removing Alzheimerâs-associated plaques, suggesting a completely different way to combat cognitive decline.
paras.zh: 一种革命性的新型鼻腔治疗方法使衰老小鼠恢复了年轻时的学习和记忆能力，同时防止患有阿尔茨海默氏病的小鼠认知能力严重下降。该滴鼻剂采用类似于 COVID-19 mRNA 疫苗的技术开发，可刺激大脑保护蛋白的产生，从而增强神经元并支持记忆。值得注意的是，这种治疗在不去除阿尔茨海默病相关斑块的情况下保留了大脑功能，这表明了一种完全不同的对抗认知能力下降的方法。

paras.en: Researchers at the University of Sydney have created experimental nose drops that significantly improved learning and memory in older mice, bringing their performance back to levels seen in younger animals. The treatment also prevented severe memory decline in mice genetically engineered to develop Alzheimer's-like disease. Remarkably, the approach relies on mRNA technology similar to that used in COVID-19 vaccines.
paras.zh: 悉尼大学的研究人员发明了实验性滴鼻剂，可以显着改善老年小鼠的学习和记忆力，使其表现恢复到年轻动物的水平。这种治疗还可以防止经过基因工程改造而患上类似阿尔茨海默病的小鼠的记忆力严重下降。值得注意的是，该方法依赖于类似于 COVID-19 疫苗中使用的 mRNA 技术。

paras.en: The discovery, led by Professor Greg Neely at the University of Sydney's Charles Perkins Centre, could open a new path toward treating conditions that affect the brain. Potential applications extend beyond Alzheimer's disease to other neurodegenerative disorders, stroke, traumatic brain injury, and rare genetic and developmental conditions.
paras.zh: 悉尼大学查尔斯·珀金斯中心的格雷格·尼利教授领导的这一发现可能为治疗影响大脑的疾病开辟一条新途径。潜在的应用范围不仅限于阿尔茨海默病，还包括其他神经退行性疾病、中风、创伤性脑损伤以及罕见的遗传和发育疾病。

paras.en: "If we can proceed quickly to clinical trials in humans, this approach could represent a world-first non-invasive delivery system to treat Alzheimer's that bypasses the blood-brain barrier," Professor Neely said.
paras.zh: 尼利教授说：“如果我们能够迅速进行人体临床试验，这种方法可能代表世界上第一个绕过血脑屏障的非侵入性递送系统，用于治疗阿尔茨海默病。”

paras.en: The idea behind the research has an unusual origin. The team drew inspiration from Daniel Keyes' science fiction story Flowers for Algernon, which explores the limits of human intelligence through experiments designed to increase intelligence in laboratory mice and people.
paras.zh: 这项研究背后的想法有着不同寻常的起源。该团队从丹尼尔·凯斯（Daniel Keyes）的科幻小说《献给阿尔杰农的花》中汲取灵感，该小说通过旨在提高实验室小鼠和人类智力的实验来探索人类智力的极限。

paras.en: How mRNA Nose Drops Restore Youthful Memory
paras.zh: mRNA 滴鼻剂如何恢复年轻记忆

paras.en: The treatment works by delivering messenger RNA (mRNA), a type of genetic instruction that tells cells how to produce specific proteins. These instructions are enclosed in tiny fat-based particles called lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), which protect the mRNA and help it enter cells.
paras.zh: 该治疗通过传递信使 RNA (mRNA) 来发挥作用，信使 RNA (mRNA) 是一种遗传指令，告诉细胞如何产生特定的蛋白质。这些指令被封装在称为脂质纳米颗粒 (LNP) 的微小脂肪颗粒中，它可以保护 mRNA 并帮助其进入细胞。

paras.en: Once delivered through the nose, the mRNA instructs cells to manufacture therapeutic proteins capable of reaching the brain. In effect, the nasal tissue becomes a small drug-producing factory, creating substances that can support brain function.
paras.zh: 一旦通过鼻子传递，mRNA 就会指示细胞制造能够到达大脑的治疗性蛋白质。实际上，鼻组织变成了一个小型药物生产工厂，产生可以支持大脑功能的物质。

paras.en: "In aged mice, we saw learning and memory significantly increased, returning animal cognition to its youthful prime," Professor Neely said.
paras.zh: 尼利教授说：“在老年小鼠中，我们发现学习和记忆能力显着增强，使动物认知能力恢复到年轻时的巅峰状态。”

paras.en: "What's exciting is that this was achieved with a simple non-invasive nasal delivery system that builds on the same underlying mRNA-LNP technology platform many people became familiar with during the COVID-19 pandemic."
paras.zh: “令人兴奋的是，这是通过简单的非侵入性鼻腔输送系统实现的，该系统建立在许多人在 COVID-19 大流行期间熟悉的相同底层 mRNA-LNP 技术平台上。”

paras.en: The study, published in Advanced Science, used mRNA to stimulate production of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). This naturally occurring protein helps neurons survive, form connections, and adapt as the brain learns and stores memories. Levels of BDNF tend to decline with aging and are also associated with Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《Advanced Science》上，利用 mRNA 刺激脑源性神经营养因子 (BDNF) 的产生。这种天然存在的蛋白质可以帮助神经元存活、形成连接并在大脑学习和存储记忆时进行适应。 BDNF 的水平往往会随着年龄的增长而下降，并且也与阿尔茨海默病有关。

paras.en: The results were striking. Older mice that received the nose drops performed about as well as young mice in standardized tests of working memory, spatial memory, and object recognition. These tests measure abilities such as remembering recently encountered information, navigating surroundings, and recognizing familiar objects. Untreated older animals showed the expected age-related deterioration in cognitive performance.
paras.zh: 结果是惊人的。在工作记忆、空间记忆和物体识别的标准化测试中，接受滴鼻剂的老年小鼠的表现与年轻小鼠相当。这些测试衡量的是记忆最近遇到的信息、导航周围环境和识别熟悉物体等能力。未经治疗的老年动物表现出预期的与年龄相关的认知能力恶化。

paras.en: Nose Drops Prevent Alzheimer's-Like Memory Decline in Mice
paras.zh: 滴鼻剂可预防小鼠类似阿尔茨海默氏症的记忆衰退

paras.en: To investigate whether the treatment might also protect against Alzheimer's disease, researchers turned to a widely used laboratory model known as 5XFAD mice. These animals carry genetic mutations that cause them to develop Alzheimer's-like brain changes and memory problems unusually early in life.
paras.zh: 为了研究这种治疗是否也可以预防阿尔茨海默病，研究人员转向了一种广泛使用的实验室模型，即 5XFAD 小鼠。这些动物携带基因突变，导致它们在生命早期就出现类似阿尔茨海默氏症的大脑变化和记忆问题。

paras.en: In this model, signs of Alzheimer's-related brain pathology can typically be detected by two months of age, with measurable cognitive decline appearing around four months.
paras.zh: 在这个模型中，与阿尔茨海默氏症相关的大脑病理学迹象通常可以在两个月大时被发现，并且在四个月左右出现可测量的认知能力下降。

paras.en: The researchers began administering the BDNF-producing mRNA nose drops when the mice were two months old, around the time the disease-related changes first appeared. Treatment continued twice a week.
paras.zh: 当小鼠两个月大时，也就是疾病相关变化首次出现的时候，研究人员开始使用产生 BDNF 的 mRNA 滴鼻剂。治疗每周持续两次。

paras.en: By four months of age, the treated mice showed no further cognitive decline, unlike the severe deterioration normally seen in this model. The findings suggest that supporting brain cells early in the disease process may help preserve cognitive abilities.
paras.zh: 到四个月大时，接受治疗的小鼠没有表现出进一步的认知能力下降，这与该模型中通常看到的严重恶化不同。研究结果表明，在疾病过程的早期支持脑细胞可能有助于保持认知能力。

paras.en: One of the most intriguing results was what the treatment did not do. Although memory and learning were protected, the researchers found no reduction in amyloid plaques, the abnormal protein deposits that accumulate in the brains of people with Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 最有趣的结果之一是治疗没有起到什么作用。尽管记忆和学习受到保护，但研究人员发现淀粉样斑块（阿尔茨海默病患者大脑中积累的异常蛋白质沉积物）没有减少。

paras.en: That distinction could be important because many existing Alzheimer's treatments aim to remove amyloid. The new approach instead appears to help neurons remain healthy and functional despite the presence of these deposits. If the same effect can eventually be demonstrated in people, the two treatment strategies might be used together.
paras.zh: 这种区别可能很重要，因为许多现有的阿尔茨海默病治疗方法旨在去除淀粉样蛋白。尽管存在这些沉积物，但新方法似乎可以帮助神经元保持健康和功能。如果最终可以在人类身上证明相同的效果，那么这两种治疗策略可能会一起使用。

paras.en: "Current Alzheimer's treatments largely focus on clearing these amyloid plaques," Professor Neely said. "However, just under a third of Alzheimer's patients have serious plaques but do not suffer from dementia, and these patients show naturally higher BDNF levels, suggesting if we raise BDNF, it's possible to live with Alzheimer's disease pathology."
paras.zh: “目前阿尔茨海默病的治疗主要集中在清除这些淀粉样斑块，”尼利教授说。 “然而，只有不到三分之一的阿尔茨海默病患者有严重的斑块，但没有患痴呆症，而且这些患者自然表现出较高的 BDNF 水平，这表明如果我们提高 BDNF，就有可能患有阿尔茨海默病病理。”

paras.en: "Our approach seems to work not by clearing plaques but by supporting the health, survival and connectivity of neurons themselves. It raises the possibility these therapies could eventually work alongside each other."
paras.zh: “我们的方法似乎不是通过清除斑块来发挥作用，而是通过支持神经元本身的健康、生存和连接。这提高了这些疗法最终可以相互发挥作用的可能性。”

paras.en: Bypassing the Blood-Brain Barrier Through the Nose
paras.zh: 通过鼻子绕过血脑屏障

paras.en: Getting medicines into the brain is one of the biggest obstacles in developing treatments for neurological diseases. The blood-brain barrier acts as a protective filter, preventing many potentially harmful substances in the bloodstream from entering delicate brain tissue. Unfortunately, it also blocks numerous drugs that scientists would like to use to treat brain disorders.
paras.zh: 将药物送入大脑是开发神经系统疾病治疗方法的最大障碍之一。血脑屏障充当保护性过滤器，防止血液中的许多潜在有害物质进入脆弱的脑组织。不幸的是，它还阻止了科学家想要用来治疗脑部疾病的许多药物。

paras.en: The nose offers a possible alternative route. Connections between the nasal cavity and the central nervous system may allow certain therapeutic substances to reach the brain without requiring surgery or injections directly into the brain or spinal cord.
paras.zh: 鼻子提供了一条可能的替代路线。鼻腔和中枢神经系统之间的连接可以使某些治疗物质到达大脑，而无需手术或直接注射到大脑或脊髓中。

paras.en: "This is a very exciting proof of concept for a method to deliver mRNA-encoded cargo to the nervous system directly through the nose," Professor Neely said.
paras.zh: Neely 教授说：“对于通过鼻子将 mRNA 编码的货物直接输送到神经系统的方法来说，这是一个非常令人兴奋的概念证明。”

paras.en: The team adapted mRNA technology built on the same clinically validated BioNTech platform used for COVID-19 vaccination. Instead of delivering instructions that prompt an immune response, the modified system provides instructions for producing proteins intended to benefit the brain.
paras.zh: 该团队采用了基于用于 COVID-19 疫苗接种的相同临床验证 BioNTech 平台构建的 mRNA 技术。修改后的系统不是提供提示免疫反应的指令，而是提供生产有益于大脑的蛋白质的指令。

paras.en: First author Dr. Maria Bergamasco, from the University of Sydney's School of Life and Environmental Sciences, explained that the findings illustrate how mRNA technology could be used for purposes far beyond preventing infectious diseases.
paras.zh: 第一作者、悉尼大学生命与环境科学学院的 Maria Bergamasco 博士解释说，这些发现说明了 mRNA 技术的用途远远超出了预防传染病的范围。

paras.en: "The success of mRNA vaccines showed these systems can safely deliver genetic instructions to cells," Dr. Bergamasco said.
paras.zh: Bergamasco 博士说：“mRNA 疫苗的成功表明这些系统可以安全地将遗传指令传递给细胞。”

paras.en: "We wanted to see whether we could adapt that technology to deliver beneficial proteins to the brain in a completely non-invasive way."
paras.zh: “我们想看看是否可以采用该技术以完全非侵入性的方式向大脑提供有益的蛋白质。”

paras.en: Treatment Stimulates New Brain Cell Growth
paras.zh: 治疗刺激新脑细胞生长

paras.en: The researchers also detected increased neurogenesis, the process through which new neurons are formed, in the hippocampus. This part of the brain plays an essential role in learning and memory and is particularly vulnerable to damage associated with Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员还检测到海马体中神经发生的增加，即新神经元形成的过程。大脑的这一部分在学习和记忆中发挥着重要作用，并且特别容易受到与阿尔茨海默病相关的损害。

paras.en: The increase in new neurons provides another possible explanation for the improvements in cognitive performance. By promoting the health and adaptability of brain cells, BDNF may help maintain the neural networks needed for learning and remembering information.
paras.zh: 新神经元的增加为认知能力的改善提供了另一种可能的解释。通过促进脑细胞的健康和适应性，BDNF 可以帮助维持学习和记忆信息所需的神经网络。

paras.en: The nose drops also appeared to be well tolerated. Researchers reported no major side effects in the mice during the study, although further testing will be needed to establish long-term safety.
paras.zh: 滴鼻剂似乎也具有良好的耐受性。研究人员报告说，在研究过程中，小鼠没有出现重大副作用，但还需要进一步测试来确定长期安全性。

paras.en: Despite the encouraging results, Professor Neely emphasized that the treatment remains experimental. So far, its effectiveness has been demonstrated only in mice, and additional animal safety studies are required before clinical testing can begin.
paras.zh: 尽管取得了令人鼓舞的结果，但尼利教授强调，这种治疗方法仍处于试验阶段。到目前为止，其有效性仅在小鼠中得到证实，在临床测试开始之前还需要进行额外的动物安全性研究。

paras.en: "Before we can trial this therapy in patients, we need to perform a series of safety studies in animals," he said. "It is a very promising pathway, but human noses are different from mouse noses, so we will need to test our drugs in humans before we know whether it will work."
paras.zh: “在我们在患者身上试验这种疗法之前，我们需要在动物身上进行一系列安全性研究，”他说。 “这是一条非常有前途的途径，但人类的鼻子与小鼠的鼻子不同，因此我们需要在人类身上测试我们的药物，然后才能知道它是否有效。”

paras.en: That anatomical difference is a significant consideration. A delivery method that successfully transports therapeutic substances from the nasal cavity to the brain in mice may not work in exactly the same way in humans.
paras.zh: 这种解剖学上的差异是一个重要的考虑因素。在小鼠体内成功地将治疗物质从鼻腔输送到大脑的输送方法在人类身上可能不会以完全相同的方式发挥作用。

paras.en: Nevertheless, the researchers believe the potential applications could be substantial. Beyond protecting against Alzheimer's-related cognitive decline, the technology might eventually help support memory and other mental abilities during normal aging.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，研究人员相信潜在的应用可能是巨大的。除了防止与阿尔茨海默病相关的认知能力下降之外，该技术最终可能有助于支持正常衰老过程中的记忆和其他心理能力。

paras.en: "We believe our new drug, if it works in humans, can promote general cognitive health as people age, should help treat a variety of neurodegenerative diseases, and may even increase cognitive abilities in healthy young people," Professor Neely said.
paras.zh: 尼利教授说：“我们相信，我们的新药如果对人类有效，可以随着人们年龄的增长而促进一般认知健康，应该有助于治疗各种神经退行性疾病，甚至可能提高健康年轻人的认知能力。”

paras.en: The next steps involve refining the nasal delivery technology and conducting further studies to determine its safety and effectiveness over longer periods. The team hopes to advance toward human clinical trials as quickly as the required testing allows.
paras.zh: 下一步包括改进鼻腔给药技术并进行进一步研究，以确定其长期的安全性和有效性。该团队希望在所需测试允许的情况下尽快推进人体临床试验。

paras.en: "Based on previous clinical trials, we know the components used in this study to be safe in humans," Professor Neely said. "We hope we can move quickly through the requisite safety studies and trial this treatment in humans in the next two years."
paras.zh: “根据之前的临床试验，我们知道这项研究中使用的成分对人体是安全的，”尼利教授说。 “我们希望我们能够迅速完成必要的安全性研究，并在未来两年内在人体中试验这种治疗方法。”

paras.en: Although the individual components have previously been used in humans, the complete nasal treatment still requires its own safety evaluation. Whether it can deliver similar memory benefits in people remains an open question.
paras.zh: 尽管各个成分之前已用于人体，但完整的鼻腔治疗仍需要其自身的安全性评估。它是否能给人们带来类似的记忆益处仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

paras.en: The project brought together researchers from the Dr. John and Anne Chong Lab for Functional Genomics in the School of Life and Environmental Sciences, the Charles Perkins Centre, and the University of Sydney's Faculty of Medicine and Health.
paras.zh: 该项目汇集了来自生命与环境科学学院功能基因组学实验室 John 和 Anne Chong 博士、查尔斯·珀金斯中心以及悉尼大学医学与健康学院的研究人员。

paras.en: Greg Neely and Maria Bergamasco are listed as inventors on a provisional patent application associated with the research. The other authors reported no competing interests.
paras.zh: Greg Neely 和 Maria Bergamasco 被列为与该研究相关的临时专利申请的发明人。其他作者报告没有竞争利益。

paras.en: Financial support came from the National Health and Medical Research Council, the NSW Ministry of Health, and an ongoing philanthropic contribution from Dr. John and Anne Chong supporting the Neely Lab's research. The authors also acknowledged the Sydney Imaging Facility for its assistance.
paras.zh: 财政支持来自国家健康和医学研究委员会、新南威尔士州卫生部，以及 John 和 Anne Chong 博士持续不断的慈善捐款，支持尼利实验室的研究。作者还感谢悉尼成像设施的协助。

paras.en: All animal experiments were approved by the University of Sydney Animal Ethics Committee and conducted in accordance with the Australian Code of Practise for the Care and Use of Animals for Scientific Purposes.
paras.zh: 所有动物实验均经悉尼大学动物伦理委员会批准，并按照澳大利亚科学目的动物护理和使用行为守则进行。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Sydney. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由悉尼大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。
