paras.zh: 请访问 Sling.com 查看电台可用性，并将流媒体套餐与 THR 的 Sling 细分进行比较。

articles.title: Dell earnings beat on AI strength, company authorizes $25 billion buyback

paras.en: Dell reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that topped Wall Street expectations for earnings and sales, and provided a strong guide for the fourth quarter.
paras.zh: 戴尔周二公布的第三季度收益超出了华尔街对收益和销售额的预期，并为第四季度提供了强有力的指引。

paras.en: Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates:
paras.zh: 以下是这家芯片制造商的表现与伦敦证交所共识预测的比较：

paras.en: - EPS: $9.45, adjusted, versus $6.59 expected
paras.zh: - 每股收益：调整后 9.45 美元，预期为 6.59 美元

paras.en: - Revenue: $54.94 billion, versus $49.32 billion expected
paras.zh: - 收入：549.4 亿美元，预期为 493.2 亿美元

paras.en: Dell said that it expected earnings of $8.40 per share on revenue of about $56.3 billion in the current quarter. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $7.50 per share on $53.61 billion in revenue.
paras.zh: 戴尔表示，预计本季度每股收益为 8.40 美元，营收约为 563 亿美元。伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 调查的分析师预计，公司营收为 536.1 亿美元，每股收益为 7.50 美元。

paras.en: The company's overall sales more than doubled on an annual basis during the third quarter, driven by AI server demand.
paras.zh: 在人工智能服务器需求的推动下，第三季度该公司的整体销售额同比增长了一倍多。

paras.en: The company's largest line is its infrastructure solutions group, or ISG, which makes AI servers and systems, often based around AI chips from companies like Nvidia and AMD.
paras.zh: 该公司最大的产品线是基础设施解决方案部门（ISG），该部门生产人工智能服务器和系统，通常基于 Nvidia 和 AMD 等公司的人工智能芯片。

paras.en: ISG sales during the quarter were $41.97 billion, topping an LSEG estimate of $35.27 billion. Of that, $22 billion was for AI-optimized servers, up 291% on an annual basis. ISG now accounts for 85% of Dell's total revenue.
paras.zh: ISG 本季度销售额为 419.7 亿美元，超过 LSEG 预期的 352.7 亿美元。其中，220 亿美元用于人工智能优化服务器，同比增长 291%。 ISG目前占戴尔总收入的85%。

paras.en: "We are now a different company, with Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth," said Jeff Clarke, Dell's vice chairman and COO, in a statement. He said that Dell has 7,500 customers buying AI servers.
paras.zh: 戴尔副董事长兼首席运营官杰夫·克拉克在一份声明中表示：“我们现在是一家不同的公司，基础设施解决方案集团推动了我们绝大多数的利润和增长。”他表示，戴尔有7500家客户购买AI服务器。

paras.en: In prepared remarks, Clarke said that Dell has a competitive advantage over other computer equipment makers because it allows customers to get their computers working within hours of delivery.
paras.zh: 克拉克在事先准备好的讲话中表示，与其他计算机设备制造商相比，戴尔具有竞争优势，因为它允许客户在交货后数小时内让他们的计算机正常运行。

paras.en: "That allows customers to convert backlog into revenue sooner and more reliably," Clarke said in the prepared remarks published by Dell.
paras.zh: 克拉克在戴尔发布的准备好的评论中表示：“这使客户能够更快、更可靠地将积压订单转化为收入。”

paras.en: The company also raised its forecast for AI-servers in the coming fiscal year to $78 billion, versus $74 billion expected. The company says it has a backlog of $132.3 billion in AI server orders it is working through.
paras.zh: 该公司还将下一财年人工智能服务器的预测上调至 780 亿美元，高于预期的 740 亿美元。该公司表示，其正在处理的人工智能服务器订单积压金额为 1,323 亿美元。

paras.en: "Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power," Clarke said on an earnings call with analysts.
paras.zh: 克拉克在与分析师的财报电话会议上表示：“每一份人工智能订单都经过审查，包括获得资本、最终客户质量、贸易和出口合规性以及获得土地和电力。”

paras.en: The company also sells laptops and PCs, in a group it calls CSG, or client services group. It reported $12.89 billion in sales, which was below LSEG expectations of $14.33 billion.
paras.zh: 该公司还销售笔记本电脑和个人电脑，其集团名为 CSG（即客户服务集团）。该公司公布的销售额为 128.9 亿美元，低于 LSEG 预期的 143.3 亿美元。

paras.en: The overall PC market has been getting whacked of late, with some estimates calling the lull the worst ever, as rising memory prices have led to higher device prices and consumers are choosing to hang on to their old laptops longer.
paras.zh: 整个个人电脑市场最近受到了重创，一些人估计这是有史以来最严重的一次平静，因为内存价格上涨导致设备价格上涨，而且消费者选择更长时间地保留旧笔记本电脑。

paras.en: Dell said that it had authorized $25 billion in share repurchases, and that it had spent $4.9 billion in the third quarter on share repurchases and dividends.
paras.zh: 戴尔表示，已授权进行250亿美元的股票回购，第三季度已花费49亿美元用于股票回购和股息。

paras.en: Dell shares are up over 135% so far in 2026.
paras.zh: 2026 年迄今为止，戴尔股价已上涨超过 135%。

articles.title: Trump Account contributions from friends and family pass $1 billion mark, Treasury says

paras.en: Families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits to more than $9 billion, the U.S. Department of the Treasury said Tuesday in an announcement exclusively provided to CNBC.
paras.zh: 美国财政部周二在独家向 CNBC 提供的公告中表示，自 7 月 4 日推出以来，家人和朋友已向特朗普账户总共捐赠了超过 10 亿美元，存款总额超过 90 亿美元。

paras.en: The $1 billion in Trump Account deposits come from more than 3 million individuals, according to the agency. That total does not include the government's seed money or philanthropic gifts from donors such as Michael and Susan Dell.
paras.zh: 据该机构称，特朗普账户中的 10 亿美元存款来自超过 300 万人。这一总额不包括政府的种子资金或迈克尔和苏珊·戴尔等捐助者的慈善捐赠。

paras.en: "The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a written statement.
paras.zh: 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特在一份书面声明中表示：“美国人民正在慷慨地投资特朗普账户，这代表了我们民族性格中最美好的本能。”

paras.en: "Trump Accounts are a transformative government program for American children. It is the largest government start-up in American history," Internal Revenue Service CEO Frank Bisignano said in the statement.
paras.zh: 美国国税局首席执行官弗兰克·比西尼亚诺在声明中表示：“特朗普账户是针对美国儿童的一项变革性政府计划。它是美国历史上最大的政府初创企业。”

paras.en: Also known as 530A accounts, Trump Accounts are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.
paras.zh: 特朗普账户也称为 530A 账户，向任何拥有社会安全号码的 18 岁以下美国儿童开放。

paras.en: Parents, guardians, grandparents and others can collectively contribute up to $5,000 per child per year in after-tax dollars up until the year before the beneficiary turns 18. The annual contribution limit is indexed for inflation after 2027.
paras.zh: 父母、监护人、祖父母和其他人每年可以为每个孩子总共缴纳最多 5,000 美元的税后美元，直至受益人年满 18 岁的前一年。年度缴款限额将根据 2027 年之后的通货膨胀指数进行调整。

paras.en: Children born from 2025 through 2028 may receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury. Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria.
paras.zh: 2025 年至 2028 年出生的儿童可从财政部获得一次性 1,000 美元存款。根据某些标准，也可能提供其他资金。

paras.en: Most recently, Snowflake chairman Frank Slootman and his wife, Brenda, announced they would give $1,000 to every child in Montana born in 2023 and 2024.
paras.zh: 最近，Snowflake 董事长 Frank Slootman 和他的妻子 Brenda 宣布，他们将为蒙大拿州 2023 年和 2024 年出生的每个孩子捐赠 1,000 美元。

paras.en: The Treasury rolled out temporary regulations at the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold stock donations, a move meant to pave the way for more philanthropic gifts, according to Bisignano.
paras.zh: 比西尼亚诺表示，财政部于 9 月底推出了临时规定，允许特朗普账户持有股票捐赠，此举旨在为更多慈善捐赠铺平道路。

paras.en: These rules make it more attractive for donors, according to Ben Henry-Moreland, a certified financial planner with advisor platform Kitces.com.
paras.zh: 顾问平台 Kitces.com 的认证财务规划师 Ben Henry-Moreland 表示，这些规则对捐助者更具吸引力。

paras.en: By gifting stocks, wealthy founders and shareholders can avoid the capital gains taxes that would otherwise be triggered by selling appreciated stock and donating the cash proceeds. However, it also means some children's wealth accumulation could be tied to the performance of individual companies.
paras.zh: 通过赠送股票，富有的创始人和股东可以避免因出售升值股票和捐赠现金收益而引发的资本利得税。然而，这也意味着一些孩子的财富积累可能与个别公司的业绩挂钩。

paras.en: The Trump Accounts milestone comes as more billionaires and companies pledge support to the investment account for kids.
paras.zh: 随着越来越多的亿万富翁和公司承诺支持儿童投资账户，特朗普账户的里程碑到来了。

paras.en: In an exclusive interview with CNBC's "Squawk on the Street," Bessent on Nov. 20 announced an Anthropic co-founder would make a "large gift" to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks.
paras.zh: 11 月 20 日，贝森特在接受 CNBC 节目“Squawk on the Street”的独家采访时宣布，Anthropic 联合创始人将在未来几周内向特朗普账户赠送“大礼”。

paras.en: A person briefed on the announcement confirmed that the Anthropic co-founder Bessent referred to is Tom Brown and that it is part of his broader philanthropic plan. The person asked not to be named because the matter is private.
paras.zh: 一位了解该公告的人士证实，贝森特提到的 Anthropic 联合创始人是汤姆·布朗 (Tom Brown)，这是他更广泛的慈善计划的一部分。该人士要求不透露姓名，因为此事是私人的。

paras.en: "This is the perfect vehicle to donate to the children of America, and they will receive 100% of the proceeds," Bessent said.
paras.zh: “这是捐赠给美国儿童的完美工具，他们将收到 100% 的收益，”贝森特说。

paras.en: Elon Musk wrote in an X post that he plans to give every kid in America a share of SpaceX sometime in 2027, which experts say may come via Trump Accounts.
paras.zh: 埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在 X 帖子中写道，他计划在 2027 年的某个时候给美国每个孩子分享 SpaceX 的股份，专家称这可能是通过特朗普账户获得的。

paras.en: In a separate funding announcement, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said she would donate around 2 million shares of her and her husband's SpaceX stock to the accounts.
paras.zh: 在另一份融资公告中，SpaceX 总裁格温·肖特韦尔 (Gwynne Shotwell) 表示，她将向这些账户捐赠她和丈夫持有的约 200 万股 SpaceX 股票。

paras.en: On Monday, Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, founder of Invest America and an architect of Trump Accounts, told CNBC's "Halftime Report" that more large-scale donations may be in the pipeline.
paras.zh: 周一，Altimeter Capital 首席执行官、投资美国创始人、特朗普账户设计者布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 向 CNBC 的《半场报告》表示，更大规模的捐款可能正在酝酿之中。

paras.en: "I want everybody to own shares of Nvidia, in Anthropic, in OpenAI," he said. "We created 70 million stock accounts — free stock accounts — for every single citizen under the age of 18 to do just that, and we have huge announcements coming."
paras.zh: “我希望每个人都拥有 Nvidia、Anthropic、OpenAI 的股票，”他说。 “我们为每个 18 岁以下的公民创建了 7000 万个股票账户——免费股票账户——就是为了做到这一点，我们即将发布重大公告。”

articles.title: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: Ambarella, Dell, Autodesk, Urban Outfitters & more

paras.en: In extended trading, Ambarella tanked after the semiconductor design company shared fourth-quarter revenue guidance that was well below the Street's expectations.
paras.zh: 在半导体设计公司安霸公布的第四季度收入指引远低于华尔街预期后，在盘后交易中，该公司股价下跌。

paras.en: Dell Technologies traded higher on top and bottom line beats in the third quarter.
paras.zh: 戴尔科技集团第三季度的营收和利润均超出预期，股价走高。

paras.en: Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock moves of the day.
paras.zh: 跟随 CNBC 重点报道当天最大的股票走势。

articles.title: Read The Age of Alchemy by Kit Chapman with Scientific American in December

paras.en: The history of chemistry predates science itself; for thousands of years, kings and servants relied on alchemists to concoct “magical” ointments and elixirs. That practice morphed over the years into a formal field of investigation. Chemistry is the field of science that tells us what stars are made of, what’s safe to eat and how our species will live on a changing planet in the future. Chemistry is everywhere and connects to nearly everything. As Kit Chapman says in the prologue of The Age of Alchemy: How Early Innovators Shaped Modern Chemistry: “Before the Enlightenment, there were only wizards, witches and wishful thinking,” but slowly a “new science arrived to change our world.” The scientific study of chemistry has saved lives, caused massive destruction and informed a greater understanding of who we are and what we’re made of.
paras.zh: 化学的历史早于科学本身。几千年来，国王和仆人依靠炼金术士来配制“神奇”的药膏和长生不老药。多年来，这种做法逐渐演变成一个正式的调查领域。化学是一门科学领域，它告诉我们恒星是由什么构成的、吃什么是安全的以及我们的物种未来将如何生活在不断变化的星球上。化学无处不在，几乎与一切事物都有联系。正如基特·查普曼在《炼金术时代：早期创新者如何塑造现代化学》的序言中所说：“在启蒙运动之前，只有巫师、女巫和一厢情愿的想法”，但慢慢地，“新科学的到来改变了我们的世界”。化学科学研究拯救了生命，造成了巨大的破坏，并让人们更好地了解我们是谁以及我们是由什么构成的。

paras.en: This month Scientific American staff will be reading The Age of Alchemy together, and on December 16 we’ll share our staff discussion in our Science Quickly podcast. We’ll talk about our favorite chemistry facts and the places where we encounter chemistry in our everyday lives.
paras.zh: 本月《科学美国人》的工作人员将一起阅读《炼金术时代》，12 月 16 日，我们将在 Science Quickly 播客中分享我们的工作人员讨论。我们将讨论我们最喜欢的化学事实以及我们在日常生活中遇到化学的地方。

articles.title: Slime molds beat mathematicians at complex problems

paras.en: Imagine you’ve been asked to build a new subway network for your city. The points that the network should connect at are naturally predetermined: important downtown locations need a stop, as do train stations, airports, universities and cultural institutions, such as museums and parks. At the same time, you have a limited budget. The system should therefore be as efficient as possible: every location must be accessible, while the total tunnel length should be kept to a minimum. How do you solve this challenge?
paras.zh: 想象一下，您被要求为您的城市建设一个新的地铁网络。网络应该连接的点自然是预先确定的：重要的市中心地点需要停靠，火车站、机场、大学和文化机构（例如博物馆和公园）也需要停靠。同时，您的预算有限。因此，系统应尽可能高效：每个位置都必须易于到达，同时隧道总长度应保持在最低限度。你如何解决这个挑战？

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: These so-called Steiner tree problems are not easy to solve. They first arose in the early 19th century. Although named after Swiss mathematician Jakob Steiner, who did indeed work on them, they were first investigated in 1811 by French scholar Joseph Diez Gergonne. After more than 200 years, it has become clear to mathematicians that Steiner tree problems are among the most complex problems in the field. Yet there are living organisms that find this kind of optimal network planning very easy: slime molds.
paras.zh: 这些所谓的斯坦纳树问题并不容易解决。它们最早出现于 19 世纪初。尽管以瑞士数学家雅各布·施泰纳 (Jakob Steiner) 的名字命名，而他确实对这些问题进行了研究，但它们最早是在 1811 年由法国学者 Joseph Diez Gergonne 进行研究的。 200 多年后，数学家们已经清楚斯坦纳树问题是该领域最复杂的问题之一。然而，有些生物体很容易找到这种最佳网络规划：粘菌。

paras.en: The gifted urban planner Physarum polycephalum is a single-celled organism that can grow to several square meters in size. Slime molds of this species possess neither a complex nervous system nor a brain. And yet they can master astonishing tasks, some of which we mammals struggle with. They find the shortest routes within mazes, appear to possess a kind of short-term memory and can reconstruct the connections of the rail network in the Tokyo metropolitan area.
paras.zh: 天才的城市规划师多头绒泡菌是一种单细胞生物，可以长到几平方米大小。该物种的粘菌既没有复杂的神经系统，也没有大脑。然而，它们却能完成令人惊叹的任务，其中一些任务是我们哺乳动物难以完成的。他们在迷宫中找到最短的路线，似乎拥有一种短期记忆，并且可以重建东京都市区铁路网络的连接。

paras.en: To observe the slime mold as it plans an optimal rail network, it must be lured with food—specifically, oat flakes. In 2010 researchers at Hokkaido University in Japan conducted an experiment in which the oats were arranged to represent Tokyo and 35 surrounding cities in the metropolitan area. They then placed Physarum polycephalum on the Tokyo oat flake. The slime mold grew by about one centimeter per hour. The researchers observed the single-celled organism for 26 hours as it began to spread out flat in all directions in search of oat flakes. To conserve resources in the long run and utilize the finite food supply as efficiently as possible, the slime mold then contracted again.
paras.zh: 为了观察粘菌规划最佳铁路网络的情况，必须用食物（特别是燕麦片）来引诱它。 2010年，日本北海道大学的研究人员进行了一项实验，将燕麦排列成代表东京和首都圈周边35个城市的燕麦。然后他们将多头绒泡菌放在东京燕麦片上。粘菌每小时生长约一厘米。研究人员对这种单细胞生物体进行了 26 小时的观察，它开始向各个方向平铺开来寻找燕麦片。为了从长远来看节约资源并尽可能有效地利用有限的食物供应，粘菌随后再次收缩。

paras.en: In the end, it spanned the various food sources with a network of gossamer-thin threads. The resulting pattern resembled the rail network of the Tokyo metropolitan area. The researchers wrote in a study that the shape of the network developed by the slime mold is similar to real-life networks in “efficiency, fault tolerance and cost,” which—it must be admitted—is remarkable for a single-celled organism.
paras.zh: 最终，它以蛛丝般的细线网络跨越了各种食物来源。由此产生的模式类似于东京都市区的铁路网络。研究人员在一项研究中写道，粘菌形成的网络形状在“效率、容错性和成本”方面与现实生活中的网络相似，必须承认，这对于单细胞生物来说是非常了不起的。

paras.en: Planning a rail network is challenging in many respects. Imagine designing a network connecting three cities arranged in an equilateral triangle. You could simply lay tracks from one city to the next, tracing the perimeter of the triangle. But an arguably better solution puts one stop at the center of the triangle and then extends three tracks from the cities to this center point.
paras.zh: 规划铁路网络在许多方面都具有挑战性。想象一下设计一个连接三个呈等边三角形排列的城市的网络。您可以简单地沿着三角形的周长从一个城市铺设到另一个城市的轨道。但可以说更好的解决方案是在三角形的中心停一站，然后从城市延伸三条轨道到该中心点。

paras.en: That second design requires less track material—something you can quickly verify. If the three cities are each a distance of l from each other, the perimeter of the triangle is 3l. In the second scenario, however, the tracks run along the angle bisectors to the center of the triangle. These sections each have a length of l/√3. Therefore, the rail system in the second case would have a total length of √3l, which is only about 58 percent of the total length in the first scenario.
paras.zh: 第二种设计需要更少的轨道材料——您可以快速验证这一点。如果三个城市彼此之间的距离均为 l，则三角形的周长为 3l。然而，在第二种情况下，轨道沿着角平分线延伸到三角形的中心。这些部分的长度均为 l/√3。因此，第二种情况下的轨道系统总长度为√3l，仅为第一种情况下总长度的约58%。

paras.en: Allowing flexibility in the construction of stops can clearly reduce the overall length of the network connections considerably. But, of course, the more points you want to connect, the more complex the task becomes.
paras.zh: 允许灵活地构建站点可以明显减少网络连接的总长度。但是，当然，您想要连接的点越多，任务就会变得越复杂。

paras.en: Complexity theory, a subfield of theoretical computer science, classifies problems into different categories. It uses algorithms to determine how the number of computational steps relate to the size of the task. For example, though factoring a large number into its prime factors is extremely difficult, it’s easy for computers to check whether a number is prime. The latter falls into the complexity class of problems that theoretical computer scientists denote as “P.” In simpler terms, P encompasses all those problems that remain efficiently solvable as their size increases—the number of computational steps grows with the size of the task but doesn’t explode. More precisely, the computation time grows polynomially with the size of the input.
paras.zh: 复杂性理论是理论计算机科学的一个子领域，它将问题分为不同的类别。它使用算法来确定计算步骤数与任务大小的关系。例如，虽然将一个大数分解为它的素数因子非常困难，但计算机检查一个数是否是素数却很容易。后者属于理论计算机科学家称为“P”的复杂问题类别。简单来说，P 涵盖了所有那些随着规模的增加而仍然可以有效解决的问题——计算步骤的数量随着任务规模的增加而增加，但不会爆炸。更准确地说，计算时间随着输入的大小呈多项式增长。

paras.en: For certain problems, however, the computation time increases exponentially. Although any computer can very quickly factor the number 15 into its prime factors 3 and 5, if you give the computer a number thousands of digits long, it may give up. This is, of course, annoying for number theorists, but a blessing for cryptographers, who use such complex problems to design encryption methods.
paras.zh: 然而，对于某些问题，计算时间呈指数增长。尽管任何计算机都可以非常快速地将数字 15 分解为其质因数 3 和 5，但如果您给计算机提供数千位数长的数字，它可能会放弃。当然，这对数论学家来说很烦人，但对密码学家来说却是一件幸事，因为他们利用如此复杂的问题来设计加密方法。

paras.en: Certain tasks may be very complex, but their solutions—once identified—can be easily verified. These tasks are classified as “NP,” a complexity group that contains all problems whose solutions can be easily verified (that is, in polynomial time). The NP class thus contains all problems from P (because they are easy to solve, their solutions are also easy to verify) and also some problems that are difficult to compute.
paras.zh: 某些任务可能非常复杂，但它们的解决方案一旦确定，就可以轻松验证。这些任务被归类为“NP”，这是一个复杂性组，包含其解决方案可以轻松验证（即在多项式时间内）的所有问题。因此，NP 类包含 P 中的所有问题（因为它们很容易解决，因此它们的解决方案也很容易验证）以及一些难以计算的问题。

paras.en: The definition of complexity classes such as P and NP now stands or falls with the algorithms we know for solving certain tasks. But what if someone suddenly finds a completely new way to calculate, for example, the prime factors of a number—and the computation time only increases polynomially with the size of the number? Such questions form the core of theoretical computer science: the biggest unsolved puzzle is to find out whether P and NP are the same. In other words: For all tasks whose solutions can be easily verified, is there actually an efficient solution algorithm that we simply haven’t discovered yet?
paras.zh: P 和 NP 等复杂性类别的定义现在取决于我们所知道的用于解决某些任务的算法。但是，如果有人突然找到一种全新的方法来计算，例如，计算一个数字的质因数，并且计算时间仅随着数字的大小而以多项式增加，该怎么办？这些问题构成了理论计算机科学的核心：最大的未解决难题是找出P和NP是否相同。换句话说：对于所有解决方案可以轻松验证的任务，是否真的存在我们尚未发现的有效解决算法？

paras.en: The Steiner Problem Is Extremely Complex
paras.zh: 斯坦纳问题极其复杂

paras.en: To determine the complexity of a problem, the crucial idea is to reduce it to another. In other words, if every algorithm that solves task A can also solve B, then B is reducible to A. Therefore, A is more complex than B. In the early 1970s computer scientists Stephen A. Cook and Leonid Levin were able to show that there is a specific problem in NP, the so-called Boolean satisfiability problem or SAT problem, to which all other NP problems can be reduced. That conclusion would make SAT the hardest problem in NP.
paras.zh: 要确定一个问题的复杂性，关键是将其简化为另一个问题。换句话说，如果解决任务 A 的每个算法也可以解决 B，那么 B 就可以简化为 A。因此，A 比 B 更复杂。在 20 世纪 70 年代初期，计算机科学家 Stephen A. Cook 和 Leonid Levin 能够证明 NP 中存在一个特定问题，即所谓的布尔可满足性问题或 SAT 问题，所有其他 NP 问题都可以简化为该问题。这个结论将使 SAT 成为 NP 中最难的问题。

paras.en: Yet as it turns out, there are other problems to which all other NP problems are reducible (including SAT). These problems are called NP-complete. If P and NP were to turn out to be unequal, then NP-complete problems would certainly not be contained in P. For them, there would be no efficient solution algorithm, no matter how long you searched. In 1972 computer scientist Richard Karp identified 21 problems that are NP-complete—including a simplified version of the Steiner problem.
paras.zh: 然而事实证明，还有其他所有其他 NP 问题都可以简化为的问题（包括 SAT）。这些问题称为 NP 完全问题。如果P和NP不相等，那么NP完全问题肯定不会包含在P中。对于它们来说，无论你搜索多久，都不会有有效的求解算法。 1972 年，计算机科学家理查德·卡普 (Richard Karp) 发现了 21 个 NP 完全问题，其中包括斯坦纳问题的简化版本。

paras.en: So bringing us back to the slime molds at work: planning a rail network is at least as difficult as an NP-complete problem. (We know this because Karp had investigated a simplified version of the Steiner tree problem.)
paras.zh: 因此，让我们回到工作中的粘菌：规划铁路网至少与 NP 完全问题一样困难。 （我们知道这一点是因为卡普研究了斯坦纳树问题的简化版本。）

paras.en: If you want to connect many stations, the optimal solution can require a great deal of computing power. Fortunately, there are approximation methods that bring us at least close to an optimal solution. Thanks to that, computer programs can solve Steiner tree problems that involve more than a million cities in just a few minutes. Furthermore, the problem can be simplified in practice by, for example, limiting the number of additional stations (Steiner points) to be added. After all, you wouldn’t want to build 60 additional interchange stations for a rail network that is supposed to connect 30 cities.
paras.zh: 如果要连接许多站，最佳解决方案可能需要大量的计算能力。幸运的是，有一些近似方法至少可以让我们接近最优解。正因为如此，计算机程序可以在短短几分钟内解决涉及超过一百万个城市的斯坦纳树问题。此外，在实践中可以通过例如限制要添加的附加站（斯坦纳点）的数量来简化该问题。毕竟，您不会想为连接 30 个城市的铁路网络额外建造 60 个换乘站。

paras.en: Still, it’s striking that a problem that takes computer scientists considerable time and power, requiring sophisticated algorithms and powerful hardware, can be resolved by Physarum polycephalum within a few hours.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，令人惊讶的是，一个需要计算机科学家花费大量时间和精力、需要复杂算法和强大硬件的问题，可以通过多头绒泡菌在几个小时内解决。

paras.zh: 本文最初发表于 Spektrum der Wissenschaft 并经许可转载。它是在人工智能的帮助下从德语原文翻译而来，并由我们的编辑审阅。

articles.title: Secrecy surrounds claims of Russia’s push for nukes in space

paras.en: Recent media reports—allegedly based on assessments from Western intelligence agencies—that Russia is planning to launch an antisatellite nuclear weapon into orbit by the end of the year are raising alarm around the globe. Although these claims have yet to be corroborated, several experts warn that the threat such a move would pose cannot be underestimated and that the situation should be taken seriously.
paras.zh: 最近的媒体报道（据称是根据西方情报机构的评估）称，俄罗斯计划在今年年底前将反卫星核武器送入轨道，这引起了全球的警惕。尽管这些说法尚未得到证实，但一些专家警告称，此举所造成的威胁不容低估，应认真对待这一情况。

paras.en: Russia supposedly took a significant step toward deploying a space-based nuclear weapon with its launch of a satellite named Kosmos 2553 in 2022. That satellite is believed to now be nonoperational after it was reported to be spinning out of control last year. According to a joint investigation by multiple German news agencies, the “new” satellite is called Sputnik-S and is presently stored in the Moscow area, where it has been awaiting launch for years. Whether the Russian military is actually preparing to put a working nuclear weapon into orbit—or merely to continue conducting tests along the lines of Kosmos 2553—is unknown, says Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability at the Secure World Foundation.
paras.zh: 据推测，俄罗斯在 2022 年发射了一颗名为 Kosmos 2553 的卫星，朝着部署天基核武器迈出了重要一步。据报道，该卫星去年失控旋转，目前据信已无法运行。据德国多家新闻机构联合调查，这颗“新”卫星被称为Sputnik-S，目前存放在莫斯科地区，已在那里等待发射多年。安全世界基金会太空安全与稳定部首席主任维多利亚·萨姆森表示，俄罗斯军方是否真的准备将正在运行的核武器送入轨道，或者只是继续按照 Kosmos 2553 的方式进行测试，目前还不得而知。

paras.en: “It is possible that they’re thinking about doing it; it’s possible they're thinking about doing a replacement to Kosmos 2553,” she says, adding that she is not privy to classified intelligence reports. “It’s possible they’re not doing anything.” Such sweeping situational uncertainties are the norm for civil sources speculating on secretive, highly classified military activities in space.
paras.zh: “他们可能正在考虑这样做；也可能他们正在考虑更换 Kosmos 2553，”她说，并补充说她不了解机密情报报告。 “他们可能什么也没做。”这种广泛的局势不确定性是民间人士猜测太空中秘密、高度机密军事活动的常态。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Actually placing a nuclear weapon in space would be a violation of the Outer Space Treaty, which currently has 118 countries as signatories, including Russia. Not only would launching the weapon be illegal, but its potential use would also be “relatively impractical,” says Mark Melamed, deputy vice president for the global nuclear policy program at the Nuclear Threat Initiative.
paras.zh: 实际上在太空放置核武器将违反《外层空间条约》，该条约目前有 118 个国家签署，其中包括俄罗斯。核威胁倡议全球核政策项目副总裁马克·梅拉梅德表示，发射这种武器不仅是非法的，而且其潜在用途也“相对不切实际”。

paras.en: “The use of a nuclear weapon in space would cause widespread and very indiscriminate damage, so it’s bad for everybody,” he says. “It’s not a capability that can be targeted against any specific adversary.”
paras.zh: “在太空使用核武器会造成广泛且非常不分青红皂白的损害，所以这对每个人都不好，”他说。 “这不是一种可以针对任何特定对手的能力。”

paras.en: The immediate impact of a nuclear detonation in orbit would be a sensor-frying flash of optical light, x-rays, and gamma rays blinding and disabling any satellite within line of sight, Samson says. Next would come an expanding, drifting cloud of radioactive plasma that would rapidly incapacitate most satellites that passed through it, regardless of their nation of origin or function. The lingering radiation would, depending on the size and altitude of the detonation and various other factors, make a huge part of low-Earth orbit a no-go zone for satellites for the better part of a year, she says.
paras.zh: 萨姆森说，轨道上核爆炸的直接影响将是光学闪光、X射线和伽马射线对传感器的炸毁，使视线内的任何卫星致盲和瘫痪。接下来会出现不断扩大的、漂移的放射性等离子体云，它会迅速使大多数经过它的卫星丧失能力，无论它们的原产国或功能如何。她说，根据爆炸的大小和高度以及各种其他因素，挥之不去的辐射将使近地轨道的很大一部分在一年的大部分时间里成为卫星的禁区。

paras.en: That’s not even factoring in the countless pieces of debris, all traveling at thousands of miles per hour, that would result from dead satellites crashing into one another and pose additional threats to any remaining active satellites in their path.
paras.zh: 这甚至还没有考虑到无数的碎片，所有这些碎片都以每小时数千英里的速度传播，这些碎片是由于失效的卫星相互撞击而产生的，并对路径上任何剩余的活跃卫星构成额外的威胁。

paras.en: While their use is extremely problematic—to say the least—putting nuclear weapons into orbit is, in principle, as simple as a rocket launch. And it has, in fact, been done before: At the height of the Cold War, in the late 1950s and early 1960s, the U.S. and the Soviet Union alike experimented with nuclear explosions in space. The U.S.’s notorious 1962 “Starship Prime” test detonated a nuclear bomb some 250 miles above Earth, knocking out several of the small number of satellites in orbit at that time and causing blackouts on the ground below.
paras.zh: 虽然核武器的使用存在极大的问题——至少可以说——但原则上，将核武器送入轨道就像火箭发射一样简单。事实上，这种事以前就有人做过：在冷战最激烈的时期，即 20 世纪 50 年代末和 1960 年代初，美国和苏联都曾在太空进行过核爆炸实验。美国 1962 年臭名昭著的“星舰 Prime”试验在地球上空约 250 英里处引爆了一枚核弹，摧毁了当时在轨运行的少数卫星，并导致地面停电。

paras.en: Besides the prohibitions of the Outer Space Treaty, the enormous risks and drawbacks of such weapons in space has limited their use ever since—until now, perhaps. The rise of massive megaconstellations of satellites, such as those belonging to SpaceX’s Starlink system, may have changed the equation. The Starlink service has proved vital to Ukraine’s homeland defense against Russia, which began a full-scale invasion of its neighbor in 2022 and has suffered grievous battlefield losses in subsequent years.
paras.zh: 除了《外层空间条约》的禁止之外，此类武器在太空中的巨大风险和缺点自此限制了它们的使用——也许直到现在。巨型卫星星座（例如属于 SpaceX 星链系统的卫星）的崛起可能改变了这一现状。事实证明，星链服务对于乌克兰抵御俄罗斯的国土防御至关重要。俄罗斯于 2022 年开始全面入侵其邻国，并在随后的几年中遭受了严重的战场损失。

paras.en: “If you were to put a weapon into space, it’s because you want to get rid of a lot of satellites all at once” while still creating a lot of indiscriminate collateral damage, Samson says.
paras.zh: 萨姆森说：“如果你要将武器放入太空，那是因为你想一次性消灭很多卫星”，同时仍然造成大量不加区别的附带损害。

paras.en: “That's why ... I think [it] is very low-probability they would actually do it, because I think it'd be very escalatory,” she adds. “But it’s one of those low-probability, high-impact type of scenarios.”
paras.zh: “这就是为什么......我认为他们实际上这样做的可能性非常低，因为我认为这会非常升级，”她补充道。 “但这是一种低概率、高影响力的场景。”

paras.en: The effects would be felt globally because the loss of a large number of telecommunications satellites would heavily impact access to the Internet. One modern convenience would possibly survive, however.
paras.zh: 全球都会受到影响，因为大量电信卫星的损失将严重影响互联网的访问。然而，一种现代便利设施可能会幸存下来。

paras.en: “I’m not so sure GPS [global positioning system] satellites would be affected, just because there are a few satellites that are protected against nuclear radiation,” Samson says. “These things are usually military satellites that are intended to operate in times of conflict.”
paras.zh: “我不太确定 GPS（全球定位系统）卫星是否会受到影响，只是因为有一些卫星受到了核辐射的保护，”萨姆森说。 “这些东西通常是军事卫星，旨在在冲突时期运行。”

paras.en: Nuclear bombs are far from the weapon of choice in space, where many other, less extreme options exist. The U.S., Russia, China and India have all conducted tests of antisatellite missiles launched from terrestrial bases across the past two decades. And in September a high-ranking official at the U.S. Air Force announced the U.S. had already placed “on-orbit space control” weapons around Earth. Melamed says the timing does not seem to indicate that Russia’s possible decision to place nuclear weapons in orbit would have been a direct response to such actions.
paras.zh: 核弹远不是太空中的首选武器，太空中还存在许多其他不那么极端的选择。过去二十年来，美国、俄罗斯、中国和印度都进行过从地面基地发射的反卫星导弹试验。 9月，美国空军的一位高级官员宣布，美国已经在地球周围部署了“在轨太空控制”武器。梅拉梅德表示，这一时机似乎并不表明俄罗斯将核武器送入轨道的可能决定是对此类行动的直接回应。

paras.en: “I definitely think we are in a period of military competition in outer space; that's undeniable. And I think the comments in September by the Air Force secretary are a reflection of that reality rather the launch of a new phase of that competition” Melamed says. “I don’t think it’s fair to link this latest reporting around the Russian capability to that announcement because this Russian capability, at least the reporting on it, is that they were developing this capability back in 2024, and who knows how long before that the intelligence might have existed.”
paras.zh: “我绝对认为我们正处于外太空军事竞争时期；这是不可否认的。我认为空军部长 9 月份的评论反映了这一现实，而不是启动了该竞争的新阶段”梅拉梅德说。 “我认为将有关俄罗斯能力的最新报道与该声明联系起来是不公平的，因为俄罗斯的能力，至少是有关它的报道，是他们早在 2024 年就正在开发这种能力，谁知道情报可能已经存在多久了。”

paras.en: The potential decision to launch a nuclear weapon into space may instead just be an effort for Russia to project power and reclaim its position as a force to be reckoned with.
paras.zh: 相反，向太空发射核武器的潜在决定可能只是俄罗斯投射力量并重新夺回其不可忽视力量地位的努力。

paras.en: “Russia has a historical legacy of being a major space power going back from the Soviet times,” Samson says. “This is something they’re very proud of. I don’t think it’s something they’d give up lightly.”
paras.zh: “俄罗斯自苏联时代起就拥有作为主要太空强国的历史遗产，”萨姆森说。 “这是他们非常自豪的事情。我不认为这是他们会轻易放弃的事情。”

articles.title: How do scientists learn from failure? This researcher has clues
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Yian Yin seeks to understand the dynamics of science itself. The computational social scientist is particularly interested in how innovations happen and how they may be accelerated.
paras.zh: 尹彦试图了解科学本身的动态。计算社会科学家对创新如何发生以及如何加速创新特别感兴趣。

paras.en: “I want to understand what the secret sources or recipes of success are,” says Yin, of Cornell University.
paras.zh: “我想了解成功的秘密来源或秘诀是什么，”康奈尔大学的尹说。

paras.en: He applied machine learning techniques to accepted and rejected research proposals to understand how scientists learn from failures. What he found was that scientists fail, and they fail often. Some switched gears after some rejections, but others who continued their research and incorporated feedback found success at a faster rate. Those who changed ideas or scrapped original proposals did not leverage a lot from their experience.
paras.zh: 他将机器学习技术应用于接受和拒绝的研究提案，以了解科学家如何从失败中学习。他发现科学家会失败，而且他们经常失败。一些人在遭到拒绝后改变了方向，但另一些人继续研究并吸收反馈，发现成功的速度更快。那些改变想法或放弃最初提案的人并没有充分利用他们的经验。

paras.en: “A group that’s not only failing better and better,” Yin says, “is also failing faster and increasingly faster towards their eventual success.”
paras.zh: 尹说：“一个团队不仅会失败得越来越好，而且失败的速度也会越来越快，最终走向成功。”

paras.en: More recently, Yin has been investigating how generative AI is changing scientific publishing. Journals are receiving more AI-assisted submissions than ever before, which is leading the peer-review process to falter. More seemingly well-written papers that lack substance are getting through, he found. Coming up with large-scale solutions requires looking at the issue in a measurable way, Yin says.
paras.zh: 最近，尹一直在研究生成人工智能如何改变科学出版。期刊收到的人工智能辅助投稿比以往任何时候都多，这导致同行评审过程陷入困境。他发现，更多看似写得很好但缺乏实质内容的论文正在被通过。尹说，提出大规模解决方案需要以可衡量的方式看待问题。

paras.en: “Considering both the technological and social side of scientific ecosystems would be something that’s really beneficial for the ongoing public debate and discussion about how we accelerate science in the age of artificial intelligence,” Yin says.
paras.zh: 尹说：“考虑到科学生态系统的技术和社会方面，对于正在进行的关于如何在人工智能时代加速科学发展的公众辩论和讨论来说，这确实是有益的。”

articles.title: Eagles can prey on adult baboons. Did our ancestors face that threat?
articles.author: Jay Bennett

paras.en: As if leopards and saber-toothed cats weren’t enough, some ancient human relatives probably also had to contend with predators that swooped down from the skies.
paras.zh: 似乎豹子和剑齿猫还不够，一些古代人类亲戚可能还必须与从天而降的掠食者作斗争。

paras.en: Adult male baboon remains found in Africa carry telltale signs of raptor predation. The specimens probably weighed about 22 to 26 kilograms in life. That’s twice the size of the largest primates previously known to be preyed upon by a raptor species and on par with some early human ancestors, researchers report November 18 in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology. Guarding against aerial predators may have pressured humans’ ancient cousins to form tighter social groups and develop vocal strategies that preceded language, the researchers say.
paras.zh: 在非洲发现的成年雄性狒狒遗骸带有猛禽捕食的迹象。这些标本生前的重量可能约为 22 至 26 公斤。研究人员 11 月 18 日在《美国生物人类学杂志》上报道称，它的体型是此前已知的猛禽类捕食的最大灵长类动物的两倍，与一些早期人类祖先的体型相当。研究人员表示，防范空中掠食者可能迫使人类的远古近亲形成更紧密的社会群体，并发展出先于语言的发声策略。

paras.en: Biologists discovered the baboon bones among the high sandstone cliffs of Ennedi Plateau in northeastern Chad. These baboons (Papio anubis) have developed unique survival strategies, such as scaling 50-meter cliffs and digging for water and food. They share the plateau with multiple birds of prey, and the researchers have identified one as the most likely baboon hunter: the Verreaux’s eagle (Aquila verreauxii).
paras.zh: 生物学家在乍得东北部恩内迪高原的高砂岩悬崖中发现了狒狒骨头。这些狒狒 (Papio anubis) 制定了独特的生存策略，例如攀爬 50 米的悬崖以及挖掘水和食物。它们与多种猛禽共享高原，研究人员发现其中一种最有可能是狒狒猎手：维罗鹰（Aquila verreauxii）。

paras.en: Researchers have long studied predation from land carnivores such as big cats and crocodiles as a primary driver of behavioral changes in primates, including human ancestors. While a five-kilogram bird like a Verreaux’s eagle taking down a 22-kilogram monkey may seem unlikely, the raptors appear to have developed specialized hunting techniques.
paras.zh: 研究人员长期以来一直研究大型猫科动物和鳄鱼等陆地食肉动物的捕食行为，认为这是包括人类祖先在内的灵长类动物行为变化的主要驱动因素。虽然像维罗鹰这样重达 5 公斤的鸟似乎不太可能击落重达 22 公斤的猴子，但猛禽似乎已经发展出了专门的狩猎技术。

paras.en: “It’s pretty brutal, but it’s pretty quick,” says Cat Hobaiter, a primatologist at the University of St Andrews in Scotland. The eagles stab their talons “straight through the eye, straight through the brain, and that’s a very effective control and kill.” The birds may also drag the baboons off the cliffs, a strategy that golden eagles use to hunt large mountain goats and sheep in the Alps. The birds then dismember the prey and carry off pieces to their nests.
paras.zh: 苏格兰圣安德鲁斯大学的灵长类动物学家卡特·霍拜特 (Cat Hobaiter) 表示：“这非常残酷，但速度相当快。”老鹰用爪子“直刺眼睛，直刺大脑，这是非常有效的控制和捕杀”。这些鸟也可能把狒狒拖下悬崖，这是金雕在阿尔卑斯山捕猎大型山羊和绵羊的策略。然后鸟儿肢解猎物并将碎片带回巢穴。

paras.en: Three adult male baboon skulls that Hobaiter and her colleagues studied had clearly visible punctures through the eye sockets. And two specimens also had gashes across the shoulder bones, which appear to have been made by grasping talons. The researchers estimated the weight of the animals based on the size of the head of their femurs, where these upper leg bones attach to the hip.
paras.zh: 霍拜特和她的同事研究的三个成年雄性狒狒头骨的眼窝上有清晰可见的穿孔。两个标本的肩骨上也有伤口，这些伤口似乎是由爪子抓握造成的。研究人员根据股骨头的大小估计了动物的体重，这些大腿骨与臀部相连。

paras.en: While the punctures could come from something other than an eagle’s talon, such as a bite or a bullet, the clean circular holes in the skulls match similar damage to smaller monkeys hunted by eagles, Hobaiter says.
paras.zh: 霍拜特说，虽然刺伤可能是由鹰爪以外的东西造成的，比如咬伤或子弹，但头骨上干净的圆形孔与鹰猎杀的较小猴子所造成的伤害类似。

paras.en: “I found the evidence pretty compelling,” says Scott McGraw, an evolutionary biologist at Ohio State University in Columbus who was not involved with the work. The punctures look “remarkably similar” to injuries in monkeys hunted by the African crowned eagle in the Taï Forest of Côte d’Ivoire, McGraw says.
paras.zh: “我发现这些证据非常令人信服，”哥伦布俄亥俄州立大学的进化生物学家斯科特·麦格劳（Scott McGraw）说，他没有参与这项工作。麦格劳说，这些刺孔看起来与科特迪瓦塔伊森林中非洲冠雕猎杀猴子的伤口“非常相似”。

paras.en: The eagles also use the landscape to their advantage, hugging cliffs to stay hidden and possibly hunting in pairs, Hobaiter says. It’s possible that one eagle could distract the baboons from above while another swoops up from below a cliff to attack, as has been observed against other prey, she says.
paras.zh: 霍拜特说，老鹰还利用景观优势，紧贴悬崖隐藏起来，并可能成对狩猎。她说，一只鹰可能会从上方分散狒狒的注意力，而另一只鹰则从悬崖下方猛扑过来进行攻击，就像针对其他猎物所观察到的那样。

paras.en: While the research team did not witness an eagle attack a baboon, they did observe the monkeys responding to the Verreaux’s eagles’ presence, though not to other raptors in the area.
paras.zh: 虽然研究小组没有目睹老鹰攻击狒狒，但他们确实观察到猴子对维罗老鹰的存在做出反应，但对该地区的其他猛禽没有反应。

paras.en: When the eagles flew down over a ridge, the baboons immediately barked out an alarm call and climbed over the edge of a cliff to safety, Hobaiter says.
paras.zh: 霍拜特说，当老鹰飞过山脊时，狒狒立即发出警报，并爬过悬崖边缘到达安全地带。

paras.en: The eagles’ ability to hunt large primates suggests that raptors may have also hunted ancient human ancestors, Hobaiter says. In particular, the genus Australopithecus, which lived about 4 million to 2 million years ago and included the famous fossil named Lucy, had similar body sizes to the baboons. A 2.8-million-year-old skull called the Taung child from the species A. africanus even has puncture and scratch marks that McGraw and other researchers argue probably came from a raptor.
paras.zh: 霍拜特说，鹰捕猎大型灵长类动物的能力表明猛禽可能也捕猎过古代人类祖先。特别是南方古猿属，生活在大约400万至200万年前，包括著名的露西化石，其体型与狒狒相似。一个 280 万年前的非洲非洲猿头骨上甚至有刺穿和划痕，麦格劳和其他研究人员认为这些痕迹可能来自猛禽。

paras.en: The threat from birds of prey paints a more complete picture of how and why our ancestors developed certain behaviors, such as social grouping to protect younger animals. Primates also use a range of vocal alerts to warn the group of danger. They use different sounds or combinations of sounds for different threats, such as a predator on the ground or in the sky.
paras.zh: 来自猛禽的威胁更全面地描绘了我们的祖先如何以及为何发展出某些行为，例如保护年幼动物的社会群体。灵长类动物还使用一系列声音警报来警告群体存在危险。他们针对不同的威胁使用不同的声音或声音组合，例如地面或天空的捕食者。

paras.en: “Those first steps towards combining information in different ways to be more specific … would have been a really important precursor [of language],” Hobaiter says.
paras.zh: “以不同方式将信息组合得更具体的第一步……将是[语言]的一个非常重要的先驱，”霍拜特说。

articles.title: This man sometimes sees his cat’s eyes on people’s faces
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: After returning home from a 2024 brain surgery, a man started noticing something strange: Eyes that he had previously seen started showing up on the face he was currently looking at. To his bewilderment, the swapping of features even extended to his pet cat Luna.
paras.zh: 2024 年，一名男子完成脑部手术回家后，开始注意到一些奇怪的事情：他之前看到的眼睛开始出现在他现在正在看的脸上。令他困惑的是，这种特征的互换甚至延伸到了他的宠物猫卢娜身上。

paras.en: “Right when I got home from the hospitals, I was seeing my cat in my mother and my sister,” says the 29-year-old teacher, who has asked to go by Karl to protect his privacy. “That was one of the first things that I noticed,” he says. “And the cat even took on resemblances of people.”
paras.zh: “当我从医院回到家时，我在我母亲和姐姐身上看到了我的猫，”这位 29 岁的老师说，为了保护自己的隐私，他要求以卡尔的名义去。 “这是我首先注意到的事情之一，”他说。 “这只猫甚至变得与人相似。”

paras.en: It was unsettling, to say the least. “Looking at her and then looking at somebody else, I might see her giant eyes on a person.”
paras.zh: 至少可以说，这令人不安。 “看看她，然后看看其他人，我可能会看到她巨大的眼睛注视着一个人。”

paras.en: Scientists have now described Karl’s perception of faces in the December issue of Cortex. His condition, in which echoes of a previously viewed image appear in a new context, is called palinopsia, and it was likely caused by Karl’s brain surgery. Because the echoes appear on faces, they distort how faces look to him, a condition known as prosopometamorphopsia. The new work offers clues about how brains perceive faces, both under normal and unusual conditions.
paras.zh: 科学家们现在在《Cortex》十二月号上描述了卡尔对面孔的感知。他的症状是以前看过的图像的回声出现在新的环境中，这种情况被称为旧视症，这很可能是由卡尔的脑部手术引起的。因为回声出现在脸上，所以它们扭曲了他眼中的面孔，这种情况被称为“面部变形症”。这项新研究提供了关于大脑在正常和异常条件下如何感知面部的线索。

paras.en: The researchers’ analyses of the man’s face perceptions are “wonderfully innovative,” says clinical psychiatrist Jan Dirk Blom of Leiden University and Parnassia Psychiatric Institute in the Netherlands, who was not involved in the work. “In this era of big data and complex statistical analyses, we almost forget how informative clinical observations in single patients can be.”
paras.zh: 荷兰莱顿大学和帕纳西亚精神病学研究所的临床精神病学家扬·德克·布洛姆（Jan Dirk Blom）没有参与这项工作，他说，研究人员对这名男子面部感知的分析“非常创新”。 “在这个大数据和复杂统计分析的时代，我们几乎忘记了单个患者的临床观察可以提供多么丰富的信息。”

paras.en: Karl’s unusual perceptions caught the attention of researchers. “His face processing system is disrupted, and it’s disrupted in a specific way,” says Brad Duchaine, a visual neuroscientist at Dartmouth University. “For reasons we don’t understand, items from memory are being pulled up and pasted onto the face that he’s perceiving.”
paras.zh: 卡尔不同寻常的看法引起了研究人员的注意。达特茅斯大学视觉神经科学家布拉德·杜链 (Brad Duchaine) 表示：“他的面部处理系统受到了干扰，而且是以一种特定的方式受到干扰。” “出于我们不明白的原因，记忆中的内容被拉出来并粘贴到他所感知的脸上。”

paras.en: Duchaine’s lab has been collecting case studies of people who perceive faces differently in an effort to learn about visual perception. Duchaine and his colleagues assessed Karl’s experiences by showing him images of faces and asking him to describe what he saw. This confirmed that he consistently saw distortions in the eye regions of faces, such as the shape, and in faces’ shading and sometimes even texture. As they worked together, Duchaine and Karl used AI-image generators to create pictures of faces that resemble what Karl saw for the cat-human swap.
paras.zh: 杜链的实验室一直在收集对面孔有不同感知的人的案例研究，以了解视觉感知。杜尚和他的同事通过向卡尔展示面部图像并要求他描述他所看到的内容来评估卡尔的经历。这证实了他始终看到面部眼睛区域的扭曲，例如形状、面部阴影，有时甚至是纹理。当他们一起工作时，杜链和卡尔使用人工智能图像生成器创建了类似于卡尔在猫与人交换中看到的面孔的图片。

paras.en: Karl isn’t the only person with palinopsia that affects faces, Duchaine says. A few other people have contacted him who also see echoes of prior faces. But Karl’s palinopsia seems different. “His were really consistent, very long-lasting. And then the cross-species transfer is something that I’d never heard before,” with one major exception, Duchaine says. A case study from 1986 describes a woman who, after seeing a poodle on a bus, saw poodle heads on every other passenger, too. That woman’s distortions lasted only about half an hour; Karl’s perceptual shifts have been consistently present since his 2024 surgery.
paras.zh: 杜尚说，卡尔并不是唯一一个患有影响面部旧视的人。其他一些人也联系了他，他们也看到了之前面孔的回声。但卡尔的旧貌似乎有所不同。 “他的表现非常一致，非常持久。而且跨物种转移是我以前从未听说过的，”杜链说，但有一个重大例外。 1986 年的一项案例研究描述了一位女士，她在公交车上看到一只贵宾犬后，也看到其他乘客身上都有贵宾​​犬的头像。那个女人的扭曲只持续了大约半个小时；自 2024 年手术以来，Karl 的知觉转变一直存在。

paras.en: “What is new about the present study is the finding that a cat’s eyes can apparently be transposed from memory banks onto human faces observed in the here and now, and vice versa,” says Blom. “And that we now have a rough idea of the brain areas making this possible.”
paras.zh: 布洛姆说：“本研究的新颖之处在于发现猫的眼睛显然可以从记忆库转移到此时此地观察到的人脸上，反之亦然。” “我们现在对使这成为可能的大脑区域有了一个粗略的了解。”

paras.en: During a surgery to correct malformed blood vessels, doctors removed tissue from Karl’s right posterior temporal area, a part of the brain known to be involved in face recognition. Karl’s experiences hint at how the visual system detects and interprets features on faces, Duchaine says. There’s an idea that humans interpret faces holistically, as a single object, he says. Karl’s case shows some of the limits of this idea, because he’s having these effects specific to the eye region, Duchaine says.
paras.zh: 在矫正畸形血管的手术中，医生从卡尔的右后颞区切除了组织，该区域是大脑中参与面部识别的部分。杜尚说，卡尔的经历暗示了视觉系统如何检测和解释面部特征。他说，有一种观点认为，人类将面孔作为一个单一的物体进行整体解读。杜尚说，卡尔的案例显示了这个想法的一些局限性，因为他的这些影响是针对眼睛区域的。

paras.en: “It’s sort of like a filter,” Karl says, describing his experience of palinopsia. “It decides on a style, and then that style is applied to everyone in my reality, including myself.” These filters can change across a day or last several weeks, Karl says. He’s even experienced eye feature swaps from a face he saw in a dream. “And that was then applied to me, looking in a mirror, and then everybody else.”
paras.zh: “这有点像一个过滤器，”卡尔在描述他的旧视经历时说道。 “它决定了一种风格，然后这种风格适用于我现实中的每个人，包括我自己。”卡尔说，这些过滤器可能会在一天内或持续几周内发生变化。他甚至经历过眼睛特征与梦中所见面孔的互换。 “然后这也适用于我，照镜子，然后是其他人。”

paras.en: Karl also experiences echoes of environments, he says. For instance, if he has visited an area with lots of potholes in the roads, visual echoes of those potholes can appear in a newer road. A similar thing can happen with shapes, he says: Echoes of square hallways or stairwells can appear in new spots.
paras.zh: 卡尔还体验到了环境的回声，他说。例如，如果他访问过一个道路上有很多坑洼的地区，这些坑洼的视觉回声可能会出现在较新的道路上。他说，类似的事情也可能发生在形状上：方形走廊或楼梯间的回声可能会出现在新的地方。

paras.en: Using AI and collaboration to help re-create what Karl sees is an advance, Blom says. And this sort of collaboration between scientist and volunteer is crucial. “In my line of work, clinical psychiatry, we know that everything stands and falls with the descriptions that our patients give us,” he says. “In my opinion, this is patient participation at its best.”
paras.zh: 布洛姆说，利用人工智能和协作来帮助重建卡尔所看到的东西是一种进步。科学家和志愿者之间的这种合作至关重要。 “在我的临床精神病学工作中，我们知道一切的成败都取决于患者向我们提供的描述，”他说。 “在我看来，这是最好的患者参与。”

articles.title: Scientists Have 'Resurrected' 12 Coral Species on The Great Barrier Reef
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: The Great Barrier Reef has an even wider diversity of corals than we knew, according to a new genetic analysis that has led to 12 Acropora species being 'resurrected'.
paras.zh: 根据一项新的基因分析，大堡礁的珊瑚多样性比我们所知的还要广泛，该分析已导致 12 种鹿角珊瑚物种“复活”。

paras.en: The research is published in the journal Invertebrate Systematics.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《无脊椎动物系统学》杂志上。

paras.en: Before gene sequencing technology came along, it was tricky to know where one species ended and another began.
paras.zh: 在基因测序技术出现之前，要知道一个物种在哪里结束、另一个物种从哪里开始是很困难的。

paras.en: All that 19th- and 20th-century scientists had to work with was the visual information from the specimens they collected on field trips. Pieces of coral were dragged up, left in the Sun, and bathed in household bleach to remove their living tissue, leaving behind only the crystalline aragonite coral 'skeleton'.
paras.zh: 19 世纪和 20 世纪的科学家所需要处理的只是他们在实地考察中收集的标本的视觉信息。珊瑚碎片被拖上来，放在阳光下，然后用家用漂白剂浸泡，以去除它们的活体组织，只留下结晶文石珊瑚“骨架”。

paras.en: Scientists studied the shape of these coral skeletons closely, comparing bleached pieces to a single 'type specimen' to decide if it was a match.
paras.zh: 科学家们仔细研究了这些珊瑚骨骼的形状，将漂白的碎片与单个“典型标本”进行比较，以确定它们是否匹配。

paras.en: "When you're holding that [type specimen], that's when you're 100 percent sure you're holding that species," Queensland Museum's principal scientist Peter Cowman told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 昆士兰博物馆首席科学家彼得·考曼 (Peter Cowman) 告诉 ScienceAlert：“当你持有该[模式标本]时，就表示你 100% 确定持有该物种。”

paras.en: The Queensland Museum in Australia holds one of the world's largest collections of coral specimens.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚昆士兰博物馆拥有世界上最大的珊瑚标本收藏之一。

paras.en: But the skeletons that make up that collection pose a problem for modern scientists trying to improve our knowledge of coral species. Coral skeletons don't contain DNA, so it's impossible to use the old museum specimens for genetic analysis.
paras.zh: 但构成该集合的骨骼给试图提高我们对珊瑚物种了解的现代科学家提出了一个问题。珊瑚骨骼不含DNA，因此不可能使用旧的博物馆标本进行基因分析。

paras.en: In the late 20th century, a new batch of scientists reviewed the many coral specimens in the archives, and in many cases, decided there was too much overlap.
paras.zh: 20 世纪末，新一批科学家审查了档案中的许多珊瑚标本，并在许多情况下认为存在太多重叠。

paras.en: Corals that had been given different names – and therefore separate identities – were in fact members of the same species, they thought.
paras.zh: 他们认为，被赋予不同名称（因此具有不同身份）的珊瑚实际上是同一物种的成员。

paras.en: Many species were merged in this 'synonymization' process, without the help of DNA.
paras.zh: 许多物种在这个“同义化”过程中融合在一起，而无需 DNA 的帮助。

paras.en: But the new research, led by Augustine Crosbie of James Cook University in Australia, confirms that 12 Acropora corals were distinct species all along.
paras.zh: 但由澳大利亚詹姆斯库克大学的 Augustine Crosbie 领导的这项新研究证实，12 种鹿角珊瑚一直都是不同的物种。

paras.en: Four more corals whose identities had remained a mystery have now also been recognized as valid species.
paras.zh: 另外四种珊瑚的身份一直是个谜，现在也被认为是有效的物种。

paras.en: To get the DNA evidence they needed, the scientists had to retrace the steps of their predecessors, right back to the corals' places of origin.
paras.zh: 为了获得所需的 DNA 证据，科学家们必须追溯前人的脚步，回到珊瑚的起源地。

paras.en: "Now what we're doing is we're taking that little branch off it as a tissue sample that we store in ethanol, in an ultra-low freezer, to keep for a long time," Cowman explained.
paras.zh: “现在我们正在做的就是从它身上取下那根小树枝作为组织样本，然后将其储存在超低温冰箱的乙醇中，以便长期保存，”考曼解释道。

paras.en: "As resources become available, we sequence these things, and we add them to our overall map of the evolutionary history of corals."
paras.zh: “当资源可用时，我们会对这些东西进行排序，并将它们添加到珊瑚进化历史的总体地图中。”

paras.en: Some of the specimens in the new analysis came from the Great Barrier Reef; others came from Fiji, Tonga, the Philippines, and Singapore
paras.zh: 新分析中的一些标本来自大堡礁；其他人来自斐济、汤加、菲律宾和新加坡

paras.en: "We try to get a specimen that's from the same type location that looks as close to the type morphology as possible," Cowman explained.
paras.zh: “我们试图从同一模式位置获取一个看起来尽可能接近模式形态的标本，”考曼解释道。

paras.en: "When we include all these 'topotype' specimens, types from the same topographical location, often they're telling us that there's a lot more species that need to be recognized, and some of these 'invalid' species need to be made valid again."
paras.zh: “当我们将所有这些‘地形型’标本、来自同一地形位置的类型纳入其中时，它们通常会告诉我们，还有更多的物种需要识别，而其中一些‘无效’物种需要再次变得有效。”

paras.en: Acropora species have been hit particularly hard by bleaching events in recent years.
paras.zh: 近年来，鹿角珊瑚物种受到白化事件的打击尤为严重。

paras.en: The new species discoveries suggest the Great Barrier Reef has a greater diversity of Acropora corals than we realized. But it also means that each of those species may have a much narrower geographical range and is potentially more vulnerable.
paras.zh: 新物种的发现表明，大堡礁的鹿角珊瑚多样性比我们想象的要丰富。但这也意味着这些物种的地理范围可能要窄得多，而且可能更容易受到伤害。

paras.en: "That matters when we assess extinction risk, monitor reef communities and decide where conservation resources should be directed," Cowman says.
paras.zh: “当我们评估灭绝风险、监测珊瑚礁群落并决定将保护资源用于何处时，这一点很重要，”考曼说。

paras.en: "The Great Barrier Reef is one of the best-studied ecosystems on Earth, yet we are still discovering that we have underestimated the number of coral species living there," says James Cook University marine ecologist Andrew Baird, senior author on the study.
paras.zh: “大堡礁是地球上研究得最充分的生态系统之一，但我们仍然发现我们低估了生活在那里的珊瑚物种的数量，”该研究的资深作者、詹姆斯库克大学海洋生态学家安德鲁·贝尔德说。

paras.en: "Knowing which species are present is fundamental to understanding, monitoring and protecting the reef's biodiversity."
paras.zh: “了解存在哪些物种对于了解、监测和保护珊瑚礁的生物多样性至关重要。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Invertebrate Systematics.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《无脊椎动物系统学》上。

articles.title: Ozempic-Like Drugs Linked to Improved Sperm Quality And Testosterone
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Scientists are investigating whether drugs like Ozempic can improve sperm quality and testosterone levels in men.
paras.zh: 科学家正在研究 Ozempic 等药物是否可以改善男性精子质量和睾酮水平。

paras.en: GLP-1 drugs such as semaglutide (the active ingredient in Ozempic) were originally designed to treat type 2 diabetes and are now popularly used for weight loss.
paras.zh: GLP-1 药物，如索马鲁肽（Ozempic 的活性成分）最初设计用于治疗 2 型糖尿病，现在广泛用于减肥。

paras.en: But that isn't where their benefits end.
paras.zh: 但这并不是他们的好处结束的地方。

paras.en: A study of 108 men with obesity and/or type 2 diabetes has now found that semaglutide and liraglutide (brand name Victoza) may do more than reduce food cravings and regulate blood sugar.
paras.zh: 一项对 108 名患有肥胖症和/或 2 型糖尿病的男性进行的研究现已发现，索马鲁肽和利拉鲁肽（商品名 Victoza）不仅可以减少对食物的渴望和调节血糖。

paras.en: The results, published in Biomedicines, provide evidence that GLP-1 drugs could possibly affect a crucial aspect of male fertility: sperm.
paras.zh: 发表在《Biomedicines》上的研究结果提供了证据，证明 GLP-1 药物可能会影响男性生育能力的一个重要方面：精子。

paras.en: Among male participants, sperm concentrations increased significantly after a year on a GLP-1 drug.
paras.zh: 在男性参与者中，服用 GLP-1 药物一年后，精子浓度显着增加。

paras.en: Before treatment, just over 3 percent of sperm sampled showed a normal shape. After 12 months of treatment, however, this increased to about 4.5 percent.
paras.zh: 在治疗之前，只有超过 3% 的精子样本显示出正常形状。然而，经过 12 个月的治疗后，这一数字增加至约 4.5%。

paras.en: What's more, the percentage of sperm that can swim forward also increased from 23 percent to 38 percent.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，能够向前游动的精子比例也从23%增加到38%。

paras.en: Sperm don't have to be perfectly shaped to fertilize an egg, but these factors are telling markers of quality and function.
paras.zh: 精子的形状不一定要完美才能使卵子受精，但这些因素是质量和功能的标志。

paras.en: "To our knowledge," the study authors write, "this is among the larger prospective series reporting semen outcomes over a full year of GLP-1 [receptor agonist] exposure."
paras.zh: 研究作者写道：“据我们所知，这是报告接触 GLP-1（受体激动剂）一整年精液结果的较大前瞻性系列之一。”

paras.en: Researchers still do not yet know all the ways in which Ozempic-like drugs work in the body, and what their effects on a person's health might be.
paras.zh: 研究人员仍然不知道类臭氧药物在体内发挥作用的所有方式，以及它们对人体健康可能产生的影响。

paras.en: Fertility is just one avenue of future research.
paras.zh: 生育能力只是未来研究的途径之一。

paras.en: One particularly interesting outcome of this recent study, however, had to do with sex hormones.
paras.zh: 然而，最近这项研究的一个特别有趣的结果与性激素有关。

paras.en: After starting GLP-1 drugs, average testosterone levels increased by about 30 percent and estradiol levels fell.
paras.zh: 开始使用 GLP-1 药物后，平均睾酮水平增加了约 30%，雌二醇水平下降。

paras.en: This could be a product of the cohort's weight loss. Some recent studies, for instance, have found that visceral fat may be a bigger driver of low testosterone levels than aging.
paras.zh: 这可能是该群体体重减轻的结果。例如，最近的一些研究发现，与衰老相比，内脏脂肪可能是睾酮水平低下的更大驱动因素。

paras.en: But in the current study, after accounting for factors including age and diabetes status, a change in BMI was not aligned with sperm concentration.
paras.zh: 但在当前的研究中，在考虑了年龄和糖尿病状况等因素后，体重指数的变化与精子浓度并不一致。

paras.en: This may be because BMI is not a reliable measurement of visceral fat.
paras.zh: 这可能是因为 BMI 并不是内脏脂肪的可靠测量方法。

paras.en: "Whether GLP-1 [receptor agonists] also act directly on the testis cannot be determined from our data," admit the authors.
paras.zh: “我们的数据无法确定 GLP-1 [受体激动剂] 是否也直接作用于睾丸，”作者承认。

paras.en: Scientists have found functional GLP-1 receptors on human spermatozoa. Plus, in mouse models of obesity, initial evidence suggests that these drugs can protect the testes from damage.
paras.zh: 科学家在人类精子上发现了功能性 GLP-1 受体。此外，在肥胖小鼠模型中，初步证据表明这些药物可以保护睾丸免受损害。

paras.en: Perhaps GLP-1 drugs affect inflammation or oxidative stress in the testes, where sperm and testosterone are both produced.
paras.zh: 也许 GLP-1 药物会影响睾丸的炎症或氧化应激，而睾丸是产生精子和睾酮的地方。

paras.en: "For men with obesity-related metabolic dysfunction, GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy may offer cardiometabolic benefits alongside favorable changes in laboratory semen and androgen measures," the study authors conclude, "but the present study does not justify recommending GLP-1 receptor agonists specifically as a first-line fertility intervention."
paras.zh: 研究作者总结道：“对于患有肥胖相关代谢功能障碍的男性，GLP-1 受体激动剂治疗可能会带来心脏代谢益处，同时实验室精液和雄激素测量结果也会发生有利变化，但本研究并不能证明专门推荐 GLP-1 受体激动剂作为一线生育干预措施。”

paras.en: One major limitation of the study is that researchers did not include a control group or information on fertility history.
paras.zh: 该研究的一个主要限制是研究人员没有纳入对照组或有关生育史的信息。

paras.en: This means it's unknown whether GLP-1 drugs improved a person's chances of conceiving.
paras.zh: 这意味着 GLP-1 药物是否可以提高一个人的受孕机会尚不清楚。

paras.en: Larger, controlled clinical trials are needed to determine that, but for now, they are lacking.
paras.zh: 需要更大规模的对照临床试验来确定这一点，但目前还缺乏这些试验。

paras.en: In 2025, a small randomized trial in Slovenia found that among 13 men taking semaglutide for obesity, type 2 diabetes, and low testosterone, the percentage of normally shaped sperm doubled and testosterone levels increased.
paras.zh: 2025 年，斯洛文尼亚的一项小型随机试验发现，在 13 名因肥胖、2 型糖尿病和睾酮水平低而服用索马鲁肽的男性中，正常形状精子的百分比翻了一番，睾酮水平也有所提高。

paras.en: But again, this was not placebo-controlled.
paras.zh: 但同样，这不是安慰剂对照的。

paras.en: This year, the authors of the 2025 study published a commentary on their results in Andrology.
paras.zh: 今年，2025 研究的作者在《男科学》杂志上发表了对其研究结果的评论。

paras.en: They explained that sperm production depends on intact metabolic support from cells in the testes, which rely on insulin-sensitive glucose uptake.
paras.zh: 他们解释说，精子的产生取决于睾丸细胞完整的代谢支持，而睾丸细胞依赖于胰岛素敏感的葡萄糖摄取。

paras.en: GLP-1 drugs are designed to improve blood sugar balance, potentially impacting insulin sensitivity.
paras.zh: GLP-1 药物旨在改善血糖平衡，可能影响胰岛素敏感性。

paras.en: It's therefore possible that this novel medicine could restore healthy sperm production.
paras.zh: 因此，这种新药有可能恢复健康的精子生成。

paras.en: While experimental and clinical studies suggest that obesity and diabetes are associated with metabolic dysfunction, the authors of the 2026 commentary note that "the effects of GLP‐1‐based therapies on semen parameters remain uncertain, with currently very limited data."
paras.zh: 虽然实验和临床研究表明肥胖和糖尿病与代谢功能障碍有关，但 2026 年评论的作者指出，“基于 GLP-1 的疗法对精液参数的影响仍不确定，目前数据非常有限。”

paras.en: "Accordingly," they conclude, "these findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, blinded, placebo‐controlled trials with appropriate fertility‐preserving comparators."
paras.zh: “因此，”他们总结道，“这些发现是初步的，需要在更大规模、盲法、安慰剂对照试验中使用适当的生育力保留比较器进行证实。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Biomedicines.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《生物医学》杂志上。

articles.title: US Cardiologists Issued New Guidelines For How to Manage Cholesterol
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: It's estimated that about one in four adults in the US has high LDL cholesterol, which can build up in your arteries over time, increasing the risk of heart attack and stroke.
paras.zh: 据估计，美国大约四分之一的成年人患有高低密度脂蛋白胆固醇，随着时间的推移，这种胆固醇会在动脉中积聚，增加心脏病发作和中风的风险。

paras.en: But 'bad' cholesterol isn't the only thing you need to look out for.
paras.zh: 但“坏”胆固醇并不是您需要注意的唯一因素。

paras.en: Other kinds of lipids and lipoproteins can also build up in your blood to abnormal levels, called dyslipidemia, which in turn can lead to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), the world's leading cause of death and morbidity.
paras.zh: 其他种类的脂质和脂蛋白也会在您的血液中积聚到异常水平，称为血脂异常，这反过来又会导致动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病 (ASCVD)，这是世界上导致死亡和发病的主要原因。

paras.en: This year, experts in the US updated their official guidance on how to manage cholesterol and prevent dyslipidemia, overhauling the former 2018 guidelines.
paras.zh: 今年，美国专家更新了关于如何管理胆固醇和预防血脂异常的官方指南，对之前的 2018 年指南进行了彻底修改。

paras.en: The new guidelines are still very much about managing cholesterol, but they also take a broader perspective, focusing on taking action earlier to address blood fats that can harm people's health.
paras.zh: 新指南仍然主要关注胆固醇管理，但它们也采取了更广泛的视角，重点是尽早采取行动解决可能危害人们健康的血脂问题。

paras.en: "We know 80 percent or more of cardiovascular disease is preventable and elevated LDL cholesterol, sometimes referred to as 'bad' cholesterol, is a major part of that risk," said cardiologist Roger Blumenthal from the Johns Hopkins Ciccarone Center for the Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease, the chair of the guideline writing committee.
paras.zh: “我们知道 80% 或更多的心血管疾病是可以预防的，而低密度脂蛋白胆固醇（有时被称为‘坏’胆固醇）升高是这种风险的主要部分，”该指南编写委员会主席、约翰霍普金斯大学西卡隆心血管疾病预防中心的心脏病专家罗杰·布卢门撒尔 (Roger Blumenthal) 说。

paras.en: "While we want to try to optimize healthy lifestyle habits as the first step to lower cholesterol, we realize that if lipid numbers aren't within the desirable range after a period of lifestyle optimization, we should consider adding lipid-lowering medication earlier than we would have considered 10 years ago."
paras.zh: “虽然我们希望尝试优化健康的生活习惯作为降低胆固醇的第一步，但我们意识到，经过一段时间的生活方式优化后，如果血脂数值未在理想范围内，我们应该比 10 年前考虑更早地考虑添加降脂药物。”

paras.en: In the new guidelines, written for doctors and clinicians, the main focus is to begin treating dyslipidemia earlier to reduce the lifelong risk associated with prolonged exposure to atherogenic lipoproteins.
paras.zh: 在为医生和临床医生编写的新指南中，主要重点是尽早开始治疗血脂异常，以降低与长期接触致动脉粥样硬化脂蛋白相关的终生风险。

paras.en: "Lower LDL cholesterol for longer, just like lower blood pressure for longer, results in much greater protection against future heart attack and stroke risk," Blumenthal said.
paras.zh: 布卢门撒尔说：“长时间降低低密度脂蛋白胆固醇，就像长时间降低血压一样，可以更好地预防未来心脏病发作和中风的风险。”

paras.en: This means cholesterol screening is recommended to begin in children aged 9–11 years, if they haven't been screened previously.
paras.zh: 这意味着，如果 9 至 11 岁的儿童之前未曾接受过筛查，建议他们开始进行胆固醇筛查。

paras.en: It can begin as young as two years of age, though, if there's a family history of serious cardiovascular or cholesterol-related disease.
paras.zh: 不过，如果有严重心血管或胆固醇相关疾病的家族史，则可能在两岁时就开始发病。

paras.en: Another change is that doctors are advised to use a new disease-risk calculator, called PREVENT, to estimate 10-year and 30-year cardiovascular disease risk in patients aged 30 to 79.
paras.zh: 另一个变化是，建议医生使用一种名为 PREVENT 的新疾病风险计算器来估计 30 至 79 岁患者的 10 年和 30 年心血管疾病风险。

paras.en: "With this new assessment tool, we can better estimate cardiovascular risk using health information already obtained during an annual physical – cholesterol, blood pressure readings, and other personal information such as age and health habits," Blumenthal said.
paras.zh: 布卢门撒尔说：“借助这种新的评估工具，我们可以利用年度体检期间获得的健康信息——胆固醇、血压读数以及年龄和健康习惯等其他个人信息，更好地估计心血管风险。”

paras.en: "And then further personalize the risk score for each individual by looking at 'risk enhancers', which can help guide the need for lipid-lowering therapy."
paras.zh: “然后通过查看‘风险增强剂’进一步个性化每个人的风险评分，这可以帮助指导降脂治疗的需要。”

paras.en: The guidelines also recommend that every adult have their lipoprotein(a) – a largely inherited type of cholesterol-carrying particle – measured at least once.
paras.zh: 该指南还建议每个成年人至少测量一次脂蛋白（a）——一种很大程度上遗传的携带胆固醇的颗粒。

paras.en: High levels raise heart attack and stroke risk regardless of LDL, and doctors are advised to treat it as a reason to lower LDL more aggressively.
paras.zh: 无论低密度脂蛋白水平如何，高水平都会增加心脏病和中风的风险，建议医生将其视为更积极降低低密度脂蛋白的理由。

paras.en: Whether lowering Lp(a) itself prevents heart attacks is still uncertain.
paras.zh: 降低 Lp(a) 本身是否可以预防心脏病仍不确定。

paras.en: In November 2026, the first large trial of an Lp(a)-lowering drug, pelacarsen, reported that it cut Lp(a) by 78 percent in more than 8,300 people with heart disease but did not reduce heart attacks, strokes, or cardiovascular deaths.
paras.zh: 2026 年 11 月，首次针对降低 Lp(a) 的药物 Pelacarsen 进行大型试验，报告称，该药物使 8,300 多名心脏病患者的 Lp(a) 降低了 78%，但并未减少心脏病发作、中风或心血管死亡。

paras.en: Trials of other Lp(a)-lowering drugs are ongoing, and testing is still useful for judging overall risk.
paras.zh: 其他降低 Lp(a) 的药物的试验正在进行中，测试对于判断总体风险仍然有用。

paras.en: Depending on the calculations of the new equations, doctors can consider LDL-lowering therapies – including lifestyle interventions, but also LDL-lowering drugs, such as statins – if patients are deemed borderline risk (3–5 percent chance) of developing ASCVD in 10 years, and ought to consider it in intermediate risk cases (5–10 percent risk).
paras.zh: 根据新方程的计算，如果患者被认为是 10 年内发生 ASCVD 的临界风险（3-5% 的可能性），医生可以考虑降低 LDL 疗法，包括生活方式干预，也可以使用他汀类药物等降低 LDL 的药物，并且应该在中等风险病例（5-10% 的风险）中考虑这种治疗。

paras.en: The new guidelines also reintroduce new goal levels for LDL to guide lipid-lowering therapy.
paras.zh: 新指南还重新引入了新的LDL目标水平来指导降脂治疗。

paras.en: The researchers say LDL-C goals should be less than 100 mg/dL for those at borderline or intermediate risk, and less than 70 mg/dL for those at high risk, or with ASCVD not deemed very high risk.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，对于处于边缘或中等风险的人，LDL-C 目标应低于 100 mg/dL，对于高风险或不被视为极高风险的 ASCVD 的人，LDL-C 目标应低于 70 mg/dL。

paras.en: In patients with ASCVD deemed very high risk, the target is less than 55 mg/dL.
paras.zh: 对于被认为风险极高的 ASCVD 患者，目标值低于 55 mg/dL。

paras.en: "In general, lower LDL is better, especially for people at increased risk for a heart attack or stroke," said cardiologist Pamela B. Morris from the Medical University of South Carolina, vice chair of the writing committee.
paras.zh: “一般来说，低密度脂蛋白越低越好，特别是对于心脏病或中风风险较高的人来说，”编写委员会副主席、南卡罗来纳医科大学的心脏病专家帕梅拉·B·莫里斯 (Pamela B. Morris) 说。

paras.en: "Clinical trials have clearly demonstrated significant benefits for reduction in cardiovascular events when LDL-C levels are even lower than recommended in previous guidelines."
paras.zh: “临床试验清楚地表明，当 LDL-C 水平甚至低于之前指南中建议的水平时，对减少心血管事件有显着益处。”

paras.en: Related: New Injection Slashes Blood Fats by Up to 46% in Clinical Trial
paras.zh: 相关：临床试验中新型注射剂可将血脂降低高达 46%

paras.en: While statins are the primary medications used to lower LDL levels, the guidelines also incorporate other drugs, including ezetimibe, bempedoic acid, PCSK9 inhibitors, and inclisiran.
paras.zh: 虽然他汀类药物是用于降低 LDL 水平的主要药物，但该指南还纳入了其他药物，包括依折麦布、bempedoic Acid、PCSK9 抑制剂和 inclisiran。

paras.en: In July 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration also approved the first PCSK9 inhibitor in pill form, enlicitide, which lowered LDL by more than half in trials.
paras.zh: 2026年7月，美国食品和药物管理局还批准了第一个药丸形式的PCSK9抑制剂enlicitide，在试验中它使LDL降低了一半以上。

paras.en: Until now, drugs in this class had to be injected. A trial testing whether enlicitide prevents heart attacks and strokes is still underway.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，此类药物必须注射。一项测试 enlicitide 能否预防心脏病和中风的试验仍在进行中。

paras.en: For patients, the updated advice is to eat healthy foods, understand that lifestyle changes can lower your cholesterol, and to take action early by having regular checkups, among other suggestions.
paras.zh: 对于患者来说，最新的建议是吃健康食品，了解生活方式的改变可以降低胆固醇，并通过定期检查及其他建议尽早采取行动。

paras.en: In cases where your 'bad' cholesterol levels are creeping the wrong way despite your best intentions, that's where your doctors can help – and with these new guidelines in place, that could mean changing things up sooner rather than later.
paras.zh: 如果尽管您的意图是好的，但您的“坏”胆固醇水平却以错误的方式蔓延，这就是您的医生可以提供帮助的地方 - 有了这些新的指导方针，这可能意味着尽早改变现状。

paras.en: The guidelines are published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology.
paras.zh: 该指南发表在《美国心脏病学会杂志》上。

articles.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

paras.en: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age
paras.zh: 大麻使用者更早患上精神病，而且这种差距随着年龄的增长而扩大

paras.en: A major analysis of 149 studies found that cannabis users develop psychosis an average of 2.5 years earlier than non-users, with the difference growing to more than six years among adults 30 and older. Researchers warn that cannabis-related psychiatric risks may accumulate over time, challenging the belief that using marijuana after adolescence is relatively safe.
paras.zh: 对 149 项研究进行的主要分析发现，吸食大麻的人比不吸食大麻的人平均早 2.5 年患上精神病，而在 30 岁及以上的成年人中，这种差异增长到六年以上。研究人员警告说，与大麻相关的精神风险可能会随着时间的推移而积累，这挑战了青春期后使用大麻相对安全的信念。

paras.en: A major international analysis has found that people who use cannabis experience their first episode of psychosis about two and a half years earlier, on average, than those who do not use the drug. Even more concerning, the difference becomes substantially larger with age, reaching more than six years among people who develop psychosis in their 30s or later.
paras.zh: 一项重要的国际分析发现，使用大麻的人比不使用大麻的人平均早两年半左右首次出现精神病。更令人担忧的是，这种差异随着年龄的增长而变得越来越大，在 30 多岁或以后患上精神病的人中这种差异会达到 6 岁以上。

paras.en: The findings, published in the journal Biological Psychiatry, come from researchers at UNSW Sydney. They suggest that the potential psychiatric consequences of cannabis use may extend well beyond adolescence and could become more pronounced with prolonged exposure.
paras.zh: 该研究结果发表在《生物精神病学》杂志上，来自悉尼新南威尔士大学的研究人员。他们认为，使用大麻的潜在精神后果可能会远远超出青春期，并且随着时间的延长可能会变得更加明显。

paras.en: Psychosis is a condition in which a person experiences a disruption in their perception of reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations, false beliefs known as delusions, and disturbances in thinking or behavior. It can occur in schizophrenia and several other mental health disorders. Although psychosis most commonly begins during the late teenage years or early adulthood, it can develop at other stages of life. According to Psychosis Australia, up to 3% of adults will experience a diagnosed disorder involving psychosis during their lifetime.
paras.zh: 精神病是一种人对现实的感知受到干扰的病症。症状可能包括幻觉、被称为妄想的错误信念以及思维或行为障碍。它可能发生在精神分裂症和其他几种精神健康疾病中。尽管精神病最常见于青少年晚期或成年早期，但它也可以在生命的其他阶段发展。根据 Psychosis Australia 的数据，高达 3% 的成年人在其一生中会经历与精神病相关的诊断疾病。

paras.en: Cannabis Linked to Earlier Psychosis Across Adulthood
paras.zh: 大麻与成年早期精神病有关

paras.en: To investigate the relationship between cannabis use and the timing of psychosis, researchers at UNSW Medicine analyzed 149 studies involving more than 71,000 participants. Most of the research had been conducted since 2011 in Europe, North America, and Australia, with the majority of studies focusing on people diagnosed with schizophrenia.
paras.zh: 为了调查大麻使用与精神病发生时间之间的关系，新南威尔士大学医学院的研究人员分析了 149 项研究，涉及超过 71,000 名参与者。大部分研究自 2011 年以来在欧洲、北美和澳大利亚进行，其中大部分研究集中于被诊断患有精神分裂症的人。

paras.en: The researchers discovered that the difference in the age at which psychosis first appeared varied considerably across age groups.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，不同年龄段的精神病首次出现的年龄差异很大。

paras.en: In studies where the average age of psychosis onset was between 20 and 24, cannabis users experienced their first episode approximately 1.6 years earlier than non-users. That difference widened to 4.43 years in studies involving people whose psychosis emerged in their mid-to-late 20s (25-29).
paras.zh: 在精神病发作的平均年龄为 20 至 24 岁之间的研究中，大麻使用者比非使用者早大约 1.6 年经历第一次发作。在对 20 多岁（25-29 岁）出现精神病的人进行的研究中，这一差异扩大到 4.43 年。

paras.en: The largest difference appeared in studies where psychosis developed at age 30 or later. In this group, cannabis users experienced the condition an average of 6.3 years earlier than non-users.
paras.zh: 最大的差异出现在 30 岁或以后出现精神病的研究中。在这个群体中，吸食大麻的人比不吸食大麻的人平均早 6.3 年出现这种情况。

paras.en: These results suggest that the association between cannabis and earlier psychosis may become stronger as people grow older, potentially reflecting the effects of longer periods of cannabis exposure.
paras.zh: 这些结果表明，随着人们年龄的增长，大麻与早期精神病之间的关联可能会变得更强，这可能反映了较长时间接触大麻的影响。

paras.en: Why Cannabis Risks May Increase With Age
paras.zh: 为什么大麻风险可能随着年龄的增长而增加

paras.en: Chief investigator Matthew Large, a psychiatrist and Conjoint Professor at UNSW's School of Clinical Medicine, said the findings raise important questions about the long-term psychiatric effects of cannabis.
paras.zh: 首席研究员马修·拉奇（Matthew Large）是新南威尔士大学临床医学院的精神病学家和联合教授，他表示，这些发现对大麻的长期精神影响提出了重要问题。

paras.en: "We've tended to focus on the dangers of using cannabis in adolescence, when the brain is still developing, but the risk doesn't disappear once you're in your 20s," Prof. Large said. "What we're seeing suggests a cumulative effect, where harm builds up over time, a bit like alcohol or nicotine."
paras.zh: “我们倾向于关注青春期使用大麻的危险，当时大脑仍在发育，但一旦你进入 20 多岁，风险就不会消失，”拉奇教授说。 “我们所看到的表明了一种累积效应，随着时间的推移，危害会逐渐增加，有点像酒精或尼古丁。”

paras.en: Interestingly, the analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in the timing of psychosis between teenage cannabis users and teenagers who did not use cannabis.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，该分析没有发现青少年大麻使用者和不使用大麻的青少年之间精神病发生时间存在统计学上的显着差异。

paras.en: However, the researchers cautioned that this finding does not necessarily mean younger cannabis users face no risk. Psychosis rarely develops before the middle teenage years, leaving relatively little opportunity for its onset to shift to an even younger age.
paras.zh: 然而，研究人员警告说，这一发现并不一定意味着年轻的大麻使用者不会面临风险。精神病很少在青少年中期之前出现，因此其发病到更年轻的年龄的机会相对较小。

paras.en: "There may be a biological floor, in that there is only so much earlier that onset can be shifted. In younger groups, strong development, genetic or other psychosis risk factors may dominate, making any cannabis-related age shift harder to detect," Prof. Large said.
paras.zh: “可能存在一个生物底线，因为发病时间可以改变。在年轻群体中，强劲的发育、遗传或其他精神病风险因素可能占主导地位，使得任何与大麻相关的年龄变化更难以检测，”拉奇教授说。

paras.en: The researchers also stressed an important limitation. Because the analysis examined existing observational studies, it cannot establish that cannabis directly causes psychosis or makes the condition begin sooner. Demonstrating such a relationship experimentally would require research that deliberately exposed people to potential psychiatric harm, which would be unethical.
paras.zh: 研究人员还强调了一个重要的局限性。由于该分析检查了现有的观察性研究，因此无法确定大麻直接导致精神病或使病情提前发生。通过实验证明这种关系需要进行故意让人们遭受潜在精神伤害的研究，这是不道德的。

paras.en: Nevertheless, Prof. Large believes the overall pattern provides meaningful evidence supporting a possible causal connection.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，拉奇教授认为总体模式提供了有意义的证据来支持可能的因果关系。

paras.en: "But the consistency of the evidence, particularly the strong effect in older adults who likely have been using cannabis for longer, does support the theory that cannabis plays a causal role in the timing of psychosis onset, and possibly the onset of some cases among people who would not have otherwise developed psychosis."
paras.zh: “但证据的一致性，特别是对可能使用大麻时间较长的老年人的强烈影响，确实支持了这样的理论，即大麻在精神病发作的时间上发挥着因果作用，并且可能在一些原本不会患上精神病的人中发病。”

paras.en: New Findings Challenge Assumptions About Cannabis After Age 25
paras.zh: 新发现挑战了关于 25 岁以后大麻的假设

paras.en: The latest research builds on two earlier investigations into cannabis use and the development of psychosis.
paras.zh: 最新的研究建立在两项早期对大麻使用和精神病发展的调查基础上。

paras.en: In a smaller 2011 meta-analysis led by Prof. Large, researchers found that psychosis began approximately 2.7 years earlier among cannabis users. A separate 2015 analysis reported that psychosis typically developed 6.3 years after cannabis use began.
paras.zh: 在 Large 教授领导的 2011 年小型荟萃分析中，研究人员发现大麻使用者中精神病的发病时间大约为 2.7 年。 2015 年的另一项分析报告称，精神病通常在开始使用大麻后 6.3 年出现。

paras.en: However, neither earlier investigation had enough information to determine how the relationship differed across age groups.
paras.zh: 然而，早期的调查都没有足够的信息来确定不同年龄组之间的关系有何不同。

paras.en: By incorporating a much larger body of research, the new analysis allowed scientists to examine how the association changes across different stages of adulthood.
paras.zh: 通过纳入更大规模的研究，新的分析使科学家能够研究这种关联在成年不同阶段如何变化。

paras.en: Lead author Carly Stevens, from UNSW's School of Biomedical Sciences, said the findings undermine the idea that avoiding cannabis during adolescence is sufficient to eliminate its potential psychiatric dangers.
paras.zh: 主要作者、新南威尔士大学生物医学学院的卡莉·史蒂文斯表示，这一发现推翻了青春期避免吸食大麻足以消除其潜在精神危险的观点。

paras.en: "What we've found challenges the assumption that you'll be fine if you wait to smoke weed until your mid-20s; that's just not the case," Ms. Stevens said.
paras.zh: 史蒂文斯女士说：“我们的发现挑战了这样一种假设，即如果你等到 20 多岁才吸食大麻就会没事；但事实并非如此。”

paras.en: "There's been so much emphasis on adolescents not smoking cannabis, which is important, but we need to broaden the warnings for everyone."
paras.zh: “人们非常重视青少年不吸食大麻，这很重要，但我们需要扩大对每个人的警告范围。”

paras.en: Why Even a Few Years of Delayed Psychosis Matter
paras.zh: 为什么即使是几年的迟发性精神病也很重要

paras.en: Although a difference of two or three years might initially seem relatively small, the researchers emphasized that the timing of psychosis can have profound consequences for a person's future.
paras.zh: 尽管两三年的差异最初看起来相对较小，但研究人员强调，精神病发生的时间可能会对一个人的未来产生深远的影响。

paras.en: The late teenage years and early adulthood are often periods when people complete their education, begin careers, establish relationships, and develop greater independence. Experiencing a serious psychiatric disorder earlier in life can interrupt these important milestones.
paras.zh: 青少年晚期和成年早期往往是人们完成学业、开始职业生涯、建立人际关系和发展更大独立性的时期。在生命早期经历严重的精神疾病可能会中断这些重要的里程碑。

paras.en: "People may miss out on study, job opportunities, travel, and relationships in those years, and treatment can come with physical side effects that can make life harder as well," Ms. Stevens said.
paras.zh: 史蒂文斯女士说：“在那些年里，人们可能会错过学习、工作机会、旅行和人际关系，而且治疗可能会带来身体副作用，从而使生活变得更加困难。”

paras.en: Prof. Large emphasized the potential benefits of reducing or discontinuing cannabis use and the importance of delaying the onset of psychosis wherever possible.
paras.zh: Large 教授强调了减少或停止使用大麻的潜在好处以及尽可能推迟精神病发作的重要性。

paras.en: "It's a major illness, which robs you of your shared reality with family, friends and all those around you," he said. "If we can delay psychosis by even a few years, people will be more likely to reach crucial milestones in education and training, and develop strong support networks, which can protect against psychosocial decline."
paras.zh: “这是一种重大疾病，它剥夺了你与家人、朋友和周围所有人共同的现实，”他说。 “如果我们能够将精神病延迟几年，人们将更有可能在教育和培训方面达到关键的里程碑，并建立强大的支持网络，从而防止心理社会衰退。”

paras.en: The potential benefits could also extend to healthcare systems. According to Prof. Large, psychotic disorders account for as much as 3% of health-related spending in developed countries. Preventing or delaying the onset of these conditions could therefore have substantial social and economic benefits.
paras.zh: 潜在的好处还可以扩展到医疗保健系统。 Large 教授表示，在发达国家，精神疾病占健康相关支出的 3% 之多。因此，预防或延缓这些病症的发生可以带来巨大的社会和经济效益。

paras.en: Scientists Call for Stronger Cannabis Health Warnings
paras.zh: 科学家呼吁加强大麻健康警告

paras.en: Despite the inability to establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship, the researchers believe their findings provide sufficient justification for stronger warnings about the possible psychiatric consequences of cannabis use.
paras.zh: 尽管无法建立直接的因果关系，但研究人员认为，他们的发现为对大麻使用可能造成的精神后果发出更强烈的警告提供了充分的理由。

paras.en: "We can't run direct experiments, so we have to go with the best evidence available," Prof. Large said. "In my view, the threshold for health warnings about cannabis and psychosis has definitely been met."
